summary: Hidden. An ambitious, landless son of an Arabyan house (a daughter where the liege allows women full rights), with nothing to inherit, dreams of finishing what Sultan Jaffar began and picks a foreign realm with land in Estalia or Tilea. Only one such adventure starts every 50 years, and none while a great realm of the same faith already rules there. title: An invitation to hunt
summary: The queen goes out with the huntress, or stays at court and may pick up a vice. On the hunt she rolls her day: a great day may end in a fine solo kill, a bad day in disaster, and most hunts turn into a contest.

title: Drink to forget
summary: A queen kept from the hunt turns to ripplejuice.

title: Palace fare
summary: A queen kept from the hunt eats instead.

title: Withering on the throne
summary: A queen kept from the hunt wastes away.

title: The queen's pleasures
summary: A queen already given to vice turns to open indulgence.

title: A great hunt
summary: The queen outshines her companion and may bring home a trophy fang.

title: Hunting with the queen
summary: The huntress tells of a queen still deadly with the bow.

title: The hunt goes wrong
summary: The queen is lost in the jungle at night: wounds, maybe worse.

title: Lost in the jungle
summary: The huntress is separated from her queen and must find her own way home.

title: Who brings down the bigger beast?
summary: The two huntresses are evenly matched and turn the hunt into a contest. Picks the story and the winner; the winner hears it first.

title: The kill is mine
summary: The winner tells how the beast fell (one of eleven stories) and may keep a trophy fang. Then the loser tells her side.

title: The beast was hers
summary: The loser's side of the same story.

title: Home from a good hunt
summary: The winner comes home and stops questing.

title: Home from a hard hunt
summary: The loser comes home and stops questing.

title: Fed to Kukaili
summary: A Miyan ruler devours a prisoner at Kukaili's altar (decision eat_prisoner_miyan): any grudge against the prisoner is forgotten, the god is pleased, and the zeal may take hold (10 in 100). The prisoner learns their fate (amazon.271).

title: The altar of Kukaili
summary: The prisoner is eaten, unless they cannot die. Eating close kin makes the eater a kinslayer. A Tomb King's spirit and a wearer of the Carstein Ring go their own way (snehekharan.1, vamp.615); everyone else's dynasty remembers (the Druchii admire it, the rest hate it).

title: A vassal wants a council seat
summary: From the become-councillor ambition decision: promise to consider it, refuse, or flatter them away (diplomacy 15).

title: Reminding the liege
summary: 90 days after a promise the vassal may press again; a councillor to replace is picked if no fitting seat is free.

title: The vassal presses
summary: Replace a councillor, give an empty seat, refuse, or set them against each other with made-up slander (intrigue 15).

title: Request considered
summary: The liege will think about it; ambition.2 follows in 90 days.

title: Request refused
summary: Also used by society events for a refusal.

title: Too good for the council
summary: The liege flattered the vassal.

title: Slandered
summary: The liege claims the councillor slandered the vassal: they become rivals.

title: Land for a son or daughter
summary: on_new_holder: marks the land-for-son/daughter ambition fulfilled when the child gets land.

title: Land for my children
summary: From the ambition decision: grant a county with gold, refuse, or grant it for a favour.

title: Land granted
summary: The parent's request succeeded.

title: Land refused
summary: The parent's request failed.

title: Land for a favour
summary: Granted, but the parent now owes a favour.

title: Change council position
summary: From the change-position decision: records the councillor's current seat.

title: Choosing a new seat
summary: Pick a seat (chancellor, marshal, treasurer, or advisor); swaps with the holder if taken.

title: Choosing a new seat (page two)
summary: Spymaster or Lord Spiritual.

title: Gain any title
summary: on_new_holder: marks the gain-any-title ambition fulfilled when the liege grants a title.

title: A war is won by its attacker
summary: Marks the war ambitions of the winner. Most are judged by the loser, since the war's casus belli can no longer be read here.

title: A war is won by its defender
summary: The defender holds: marks the defensive ambitions, and the "win a war against" ambitions that a defence counts for too.

title: A rival dies
summary: Marks Crush a rival for every rival who held it.

title: A battle is won
summary: Marks the battle ambitions of the winning commander: any won battle, one against Chaos or the beastmen, one outside the realm, one at sea.

title: A murder succeeds
summary: Marks the plotting ambitions of the killer.

title: A holding is finished
summary: A temple for Build a temple; a castle or a city for Settle the wilds.

title: A holding is looted
summary: Marks the raiding ambitions of the looter: a Dawi hold, the Empire and Bretonnia, a holding of men, a temple-city, the great cities of men.

title: A title is created
summary: A duchy founded in the Border Princes.

title: An outbreak starts
summary: Brew a new plague counts an outbreak in the realm of a foe at war with the holder; Spread the Grandfather's gift counts one in another realm that borders the holder's or is at war with them.

title: A holy war is won
summary: When the Lady's faithful win an Errantry War, every lord of the Lady who held Win an Errantry War shares the glory.

title: A holy war fails
summary: A Black Crusade breaks: the defender may have held Break the Black Crusade, and the lords of Praag and Erengrad who held Hold the bulwark kept them. defender.

title: A murder is found out
summary: The close kin of the victim may swear vengeance (Avenge my kin): they are flagged and the killer saved as their persistent target amb_kin_killer.

title: Living with the Rot
summary: Every half year while Embrace rot is held: the first time Nurgle's Rot is found, Grandfather Nurgle visits (ambition.455); half a year and more later, if the Rot is still there, the ambition is done. Losing the Rot starts the year over.

title: A courtier asks to lead a flank
summary: From Lead others in battle. A promise makes them grateful; the ambition is done when they command in a won battle (ambition.203).

title: A courtier asks for an empty office
summary: From Fill a court office: the office flagged when the ambition was taken (physician, witch hunter, master of the hunt or college wizard). A refusal ends the ambition (amb_office_refused).

title: A young courtier asks leave to train abroad
summary: From Train abroad. Leave, with a purse for the road, brings them back in two to four years with the order's trait (ambition.303). A refusal ends the ambition (amb_training_refused).

title: The courtier comes home trained
summary: The trait fits who they are: a knight errant of Bretonnia, a wizard's apprentice, a Dawi or Skaven engineer, an engineer of the Empire's schools, or simply a harder, wiser soldier. The ruler hears of it (ambition.304).

title: The courtier is back from their training
summary: is back from years abroad, leaner and harder than when left, with new skills and new stories. kneels before you to take up old place at your court.

title: A restless courtier asks leave to seek glory abroad
summary: From Seek glory abroad. Leave sends them off for two to four years, to come back scarred and proven, or not at all (ambition.306). A refusal ends the ambition (amb_glory_refused).

title: The glory-seeker's fate
summary: One in seven never comes home. The rest come back with scars, a duellist's name or a fortune, and one in ten brings their old comrades to serve the ruler (ambition.308).

title: News of the glory-seeker
summary: Home and proven, or dead in a foreign field. A survivor sometimes brings their company to serve the ruler.

title: A courtier seeks the ruler's company
summary: From Win the ruler's friendship: at a feast, a hunt or a long evening, a gregarious courtier makes themselves good company.

title: Kin of the murdered ask for justice
summary: From Avenge my kin: the killer is persistent_event_target:amb_kin_killer. Seize the killer if they are in reach, or refuse: the kin then swear a feud of their own, and the ambition ends (amb_vengeance_refused).

title: A courtier threatens to leave for a greater court
summary: From Serve a great house. Pay them to stay, or let them go to the court of the ruler's own liege. Either way the ambition is done (amb_served).

title: A courtier asks for a grant to trade with
summary: From Make a fortune. A grant sends them off to trade; in a year or two they repay it with interest, or skip town with it (ambition.315). A refusal ends the ambition (amb_fortune_refused).

title: The trader comes back
summary: Honest or able traders come back rich and repay the grant with interest; the rest skip town with it and take service at another court.

title: What became of the grant
summary: is back from the river ports with a heavy chest and a heavier purse. counts your grant back onto the table, and more besides, with a merchant's grin.

title: Da boss gets krumped
summary: From Krump da boss: an orc courtier or chieftain calls out their warboss before the boyz. Fight, pay him off in teef and shame, or throw him to the squigs. The fight is weighted by both orcs' martial.

title: A servant's secret
summary: From Crush a rival: a servant of the rival's household sells what they know. Spread it, or keep it for a plot.

title: A tracker brings word of a great beast
summary: From Slay a great beast. What the beast is depends on where the holder lives: a carnosaur in the jungle, a wyvern in the mountains, a troll in the frozen north, a manticore anywhere else. A refusal brings word of another beast in a year or two.

title: The beast at bay
summary: Face it yourself, weighed by martial and courage, or let the hunters bring it down. A failed charge leaves the holder wounded and the beast free.

title: The beast is slain
summary: The holder's own kill: the ambition is done, and one time in four the beast's remains are mounted as a trophy (once in a lifetime).

title: The hunters take it
summary: The beast falls to the hunters' spears. It counts, but the court knows who held back.

title: A Stonehorn herd in the Mountains of Mourn
summary: From Catch a Stonehorn: the beastmasters have found a young bull. Rope it, weighed by martial and courage, or wait for another year.

title: A priest offers penance
summary: From Atone for my sins: a priest of the holder's faith hears their confession and sets a penance. Accept it (ambition.421), or send them away.

title: The penance
summary: Fasting and prayer in the chapel, or alms in place of it. Either may lift a sin (ambition.422), or the holder falls back and must try again (ambition.423).

title: The sin lifts
summary: On the last morning of the penance something is gone from you that you did not know was so heavy. The old hunger does not come back. The priest only smiles.

title: The holder falls back
summary: The penance did not hold. The priest will come again in a year or two.

title: The vigil
summary: From Become a Knight: a squire keeps vigil in a chapel of the Lady. A squire not yet of the knightly order is taken into it as a knight errant; a knight errant with a liege of the Lady's faith kneels before them to be dubbed (ambition.431). One who sleeps through it tries again in a year.

title: A knight errant kneels to be dubbed
summary: The liege dubs him a Knight of the Realm (the order's rank-up, as in bretonnia.203), or sends him back to prove himself.

title: The Lady's vision
summary: From Drink from the Grail: the Lady of the Lake appears to a Knight of the Realm in a dream. Take the Grail vow and seek her (the order's favour; the quest itself is the order's own path to the Grail), or wake and doubt.

title: A reading from the Book of Grudges
summary: From Strike out a grudge: the hold's loremaster reads an old grudge aloud. The hold takes it to heart (amb_grudge_bearer), or the king calls for weregild before war.

title: Slaanesh's tempter
summary: From Shed a virtue for Slaanesh: a daemonette in mortal guise offers an evening without limits. Accepting sheds a flagged virtue, and may leave the holder lustful. A refusal brings her back in a year.

title: Khorne's champion
summary: From Shed a virtue for Khorne: a scarred champion spits at the holder's feet before the court. Cutting him down sheds a flagged virtue.

title: Nurgle's plague-priest
summary: From Shed a virtue for Nurgle: a cheerful plague-priest brings a feast of rich, rotten things. Joining him sheds a flagged virtue, and may bring the Rot.

title: Tzeentch's whisperer
summary: From Shed a virtue for Tzeentch: a masked sorcerer offers a secret that is only half true. Using it sheds a flagged virtue, and may leave the holder deceitful.

title: The Skull Throne
summary: From the reward of Skulls for the Skull Throne: with the fifth skull, the holder sees the Throne itself, and one time in four Khorne sends a gift (the Collar of Khorne, once in a lifetime).

title: Grandfather Nurgle visits
summary: From ambition.215, the first time Nurgle's Rot is found on a holder of Embrace rot: a fever dream of the Garden. Give thanks, or share the gift with a courtier.

title: A herd is sighted
summary: From Hunt Beastmen: foresters bring word of a warherd in the deep woods. Lead the hunt yourself, weighed by martial; it ends the ambition when the herd is scattered. Leaving it to the foresters brings word of another herd later.

title: The king is served
summary: From the ogre_eat_prisoner decision, when a holder of Eat a king eats a king-tier prisoner: the feast in the Great Maw's name.

title: The elder plans a great feast

Health: a blessing (or a cure, if sick), a robust body, new vigour, or a sickness for asking too much.
Bonds: respect, a lover, a friend, a better ear for people, a cat, or a rival for the mean.
War: a gifted warrior, a gift for leading, new arms and drills, warriors flocking to the banner, or a maiming in the practice yard.
Wealth: a thriving (or recovering) capital, new plans, good bargains, or subjects who find they were overtaxed.
Wisdom: a sharper mind, a sage at court, an owl, new insight, the Winds of Magic stirring in a human, or a dull mind for the mean.
The blessing of health drives out a sickness, and the blessed believes as never before.

title: A false lead

title: The tombola

title: A commander lost
summary: The liege hears that his commander fell. A lover swears vengeance on the slayer.

title: The fallen foe's blade
summary: The enemy commander who struck the blow may claim the fallen commander's weapon, or send it to his own liege (battle.13).

title: A trophy for the liege
summary: The enemy liege receives the dead commander's weapon, or the news.

title: Commander slain
summary: The enemy liege hears that his men slew a commander.

title: Wounded
summary: The commander takes a wound.

title: Maimed
summary: The commander loses an eye, a hand or a leg, or is scarred. A favourite artifact may be lost on the field (battle.22).

title: The lost heirloom
summary: The artifact the commander dropped is gone for good.

title: A head wound
summary: A blow to the head leaves the commander incapable or disfigured.

title: A faithful beast
summary: The commander's dog, cat, horse, owl or eagle saves him, or a common camp animal does when he keeps none.

title: Jaws in the water
summary: A river or lake in Lustria, Nehekhara or the Southlands holds something hungry.

title: The Wounds Within
summary: Years after the war the commander still carries it: drink, nightmares, coldness or rage. The servants of the Dark Gods, greenskins, Dawi, Druchii and Lizardmen each carry it their own way, and some never suffer it at all (does_not_suffer_PTSD). Waits for peace and tries again each year. add_battle_PTSD_effect in 01_scripted_effects_duels.txt.

title: Easy pickings
summary: An AI enemy commander is cut off and alone. Take him prisoner, kill him, duel him or let him go.

title: To the rescue
summary: A fellow commander saves the commander from a losing duel. Thank him or resent him. from send_notifications_after_champion_stand_in_effect.

title: The rescuer's fate
summary: The liege hears that one commander died saving another. Shown only when the rescuer fell (the other outcome never showed). send_notifications_after_champion_stand_in_effect.

title: Beaten on the field
summary: The commander has lost a duel with the enemy commander. Surrender, betray his own side for his life, or die fighting. send_duel_result_event_effect and send_duel_result_tournament_effect.

title: Victory on the field
summary: The commander has beaten his foe in a battlefield duel.

title: Clean-up
summary: Hidden. Clears the battle duel flags.

title: The AI yields

title: Spare or sacrifice
summary: The winner of a battlefield duel holds the beaten foe. Spare him as a prisoner, kill him, or give him to the gods. Sacrifice suits the bloody gods, Ulric's wolves and warbands, or men facing Skaven or greenskins, and costs piety only where the faith frowns on it.

title: A death in the duel
summary: Hidden. Kills the beaten foe and tells his liege (battle.39).

title: A duel lost for good
summary: The liege learns that his commander died in a battlefield duel. Fired from battle.38.

title: Schooled by war
summary: The battle teaches the commander more than any tutor.

title: A soldier's lesson
summary: The commander learns from his men, and his liege may hear of it (battle.42).

title: Team spirit
summary: The liege hears of his commander's new comradeship.

title: A better way to fight
summary: The commander learns a new military art, or a fellow commander joins his host.

title: Master of the field

title: The liege reacts
summary: The liege praises or punishes his cruel commander.

title: A blade from the field
summary: The commander finds a weapon among the fallen.

title: A name earned
summary: The commander earns a nickname.

title: A skull for the trophy rack
summary: The commander takes the head of a fallen foe. He keeps up to five skulls (past that he wins prestige), and a Khornate may give it to the Skull Throne instead.

title: The liege rewards
summary: The liege hears of the trophy and rewards it (battle.64).

title: A reward
summary: The commander is rewarded for his trophy.

title: Headless
summary: The victim of battle.62 dies.

title: A head taken
summary: The enemy liege hears that his man was beheaded.

title: A rival is born
summary: The enemy liege may swear rivalry against the beheader.

title: The boulder
summary: The commander heaves a boulder onto the foe and grows brawny. A fellow commander sees it (battle.69).

title: The boulder seen
summary: A fellow commander saw the boulder thrown.

title: Impressed

title: A comrade's reply
summary: The fellow commander answers, and a friendship may begin.

title: Old battles
summary: The commander remembers earlier fights.

title: A purpose found
summary: War gives the commander purpose, and a nickname.

title: The duelist's way
summary: A seasoned duellist with a kill to his name may take the Duelist trait.

title: The strategist's way
summary: A strong general may take the Strategist trait. Battlefield duel experience could always offer it; now a hard fight can too. increase_battle_experience_effect.

title: A duelist bloodline
summary: A crafty, ruthless and experienced Duelist founds a bloodline. Once per lifetime (flag got_duelist_bloodline).

title: Commander bonus
summary: Hidden. Gives commanders the hidden commander bonus.

title: The roll of the dead
summary: Hidden. Logs how many commanders died for this character.

title: Heroism roll
summary: Hidden. Picks which tale of heroism the commander hears and fires battle.101. The weights are the old vanilla ones: brave, strong and clever commanders shine more often, the sick and the maimed less. enemy army leader. Fired by on_battle_won.

title: Heroism shown
summary: One of six tales of the commander's courage, with its own versions for dawi and greenskins. Khorne's faithful offer the slaughter to their god.

title: A soldier distinguishes himself
summary: A fighter from the ranks catches the player's eye and joins the court with his share of the glory. A vampire's soldier may be a necromancer in the making or a vampire himself. With a battle omen from a seer (Mystics) the soldier proves the vision right or wrong.

title: Captured in battle
summary: The commander is taken alive when the battle is lost. The enemy leader is told (prison.81 in WHG_prison_events). Norscan war leaders, fearsome bloodlines and high warrior lodge ranks take more captives; hidden passageways in a realm wonder help a commander slip away. enemy army leader. Fired by on_battle_lost.

title: Brothers in arms
summary: A vassal commander warms to another vassal of the same liege who fought beside them. Both get the campaign friend opinion (campaign.2).

title: Brothers in arms (the other side)
summary: fought beside you in the last battle and held when others wavered. Tonight you shared a fire and found a friend in the ranks.

title: A life saved
summary: The leader sees a fellow vassal go down in the press and drags them out, taking a wound. The rescued one becomes a friend and owes a favour (campaign.11).

title: Saved by a comrade
summary: You were down in the mud with a blade at your throat when cut through the press and dragged you clear, taking a wound meant for you. You owe your life.

title: A rival in the camp
summary: Two vassals of the same liege fall out over the battle: who held, who ran, who takes the glory. Both get the campaign rival opinion (campaign.21).

title: A rival in the camp (the other side)
summary: is spreading lies about the battle, claiming your flank broke first and that won the day alone.

title: A warherd stirs
summary: A ruler in the wild lands (Chaos Wastes, Kislev, Norsca, Araby, the wild parts of Bretonnia and the Border Princes) may see a warherd rise in their capital (beastmen.2). Rare outside the Chaos Wastes, never on coasts.

title: A warherd rises
summary: A warherd rises in a province with beastmen unrest, a herdstone, or the flag from beastmen.1: a chieftain and two sub-chieftains spawn and declare war on the top liege, unless a beastmen uprising for this county is already on. the daemonic incursion events.

title: Lieges hear of the warherd
summary: A rabid horde of Beastmen has emerged from the wilderness threatening to spoil and destroy anything they find on their path.

title: Morghur awakens
summary: If Morghur is not alive, he may awaken in Anaereth (province 2296): about once in 150 years, faster when the doom is high (was MTTH on every ruler). Fired from on_five_year_pulse.

title: Morghur's horde
summary: Morghur is born with a huge horde, sized by the doom, and declares war.

title: Morghur corrupts a province
summary: Morghur (or his vassal) takes a capital: the land is scourged, his army grows (beastmen.10), buildings are razed and up to five courtiers die. on_siege_over_winner.

title: The owner hears of the scourging

title: The top liege hears of the scourging
summary: The corrupting claw of the Shadowgave has touched , despoiling it of all that is orderly and natural.

title: The herd migrates
summary: A new beastman chieftain is made for the lands left behind. A migrating king becomes independent and his old liege is saved for the heir. (beastmen and greenskin).

title: The new chieftain inherits
summary: The new chieftain receives the titles flagged migrating_away.

title: The new chieftain stands alone
summary: The new chieftain joins the migrating king's old liege, or becomes independent; vassals left behind follow or break free (beastmen.15). ruler.

title: A vassal is left behind
summary: has left these lands, migrating with warherd elsewhere.

title: A beastman ruler dies
summary: If someone killed the ruler, the killer takes the herd (beastmen.18). Otherwise the heir may face a challenger (beastmen.20).

title: The killer takes the herd
summary: The killer takes land, people and, from a king or emperor, lesser titles.

title: The liege hears of the killing
summary: has killed , one of your servants, and taken place as leader of the Warherd.

title: The herd stirs
summary: The old chieftain died in bed or in battle, not at a rival's hand. The strongest of the herd may challenge the heir: a vassal if one is fit, otherwise a courtier. Less likely when the heir has big horns or a strong arm.

title: Liege challenged
summary: duel_beastman_decision.

title: The duel
summary: Your Hordemaster stands before you, ready to defend right to rule.

title: The old chieftain is dead

title: The challenger bows
summary: pushed through the herd and stood before you, snorting, while every gor waited for the challenge. Then lowered horns and knelt. The herd brays your name.

title: Despoil land: a herd is rallied
summary: A marshal despoiling land rallies another herd for the liege (beastmen.25) and scourges the province one step further.

title: A herd joins
summary: The liege gains a herd of troops at the capital.

title: Despoil land: the land is spent
summary: The despoiled land turns into beastman land with a herdstone (beastmen.26). Only after the marshal has rallied a herd.

title: The land is ours
summary: The liege gains prestige and piety; the province takes the liege's culture and religion.

title: Spread Chaos: fame and plunder

title: The liege's fame grows
summary: Scourging and spoiling the land of you've extended your fame as a Hordemaster. Civilization crumbles under the hooved steps of the blessed children of Chaos.

title: Spread Chaos: the land is spent
summary: As 122003, for a shaman spreading Chaos.

title: The land is ours (spread Chaos)
summary: The land of is barren wasteland where nothing grows and no semblance of order remains and the herd is growing restless for new places to plunder and scourge.

title: AI marshal: a herd is rallied
summary: For AI beastman lords whose marshal uses the usual marshal actions: the herd raids, sometimes converts the province, and sends spoils (beastmen.29). action_advance_mil_tech and action_organize_raid.

title: Spoils for the liege
summary: Scourging and spoiling the land of you've extended your fame as a Hordemaster. More Beastmen gather around the ruins of the civilizations that once occupied...

title: AI marshal: the land is spent
summary: As 122003, for AI beastman lords. action_advance_mil_tech and action_organize_raid.

title: The land is ours (AI)
summary: As beastmen.26, and the liege moves the capital there.

title: Fund an expedition?
summary: The land of is scourged by a massive Beastmen infestation. Your subjects have pleaded many times for you to fund an expedition to cleanse them.

title: The herdstone is destroyed
summary: The scourging and the herdstone are removed; beastman land takes the liege's culture and religion (Nehekharans restore Nehekharan ways).

title: The expedition fails
summary: One in five failures stirs up a warherd (beastmen.2).

title: A child of beastman blood is born
summary: Some sons of beastmen are touched by the gods (beastmen.38), more often if a parent was a bray shaman.

title: A bray shaman
summary: A child whose traits please their god becomes a bray shaman with a lore of magic; the parents hear of it (beastmen.39).

title: Our child is a shaman
summary: The Gods have blessed your spawn. It shall grow to become a powerful shaman.

title: A turnskin is born
summary: A newborn in the wild lands may be born a beastman, more often when the doom is high or Morrslieb is full. The liege decides what to do (beastmen.41).

title: A turnskin in my court
summary: Keep the child, cast it out to a beastman ruler, or kill it.

title: Beastman blood
summary: A child of a beastman parent is a beastman.

title: Beastman childhood
summary: Each year a young beastman may grow wrathful, cruel, ambitious or lustful.

title: Wrath
summary: The mere smell of blood can send you into a frenzy. You can hardly keep calm for an hour before your thoughts turn to violence and carnage.

title: Wrath: the guardian hears
summary: The little beast in your care grows angrier each day, is developing a true bloodlust.

title: Cruelty
summary: Almost everyone is stronger than you now, you've only found joy in tormenting and killing smaller animals. But one day...

title: Cruelty: the guardian hears
summary: The little beast in your care is developing a petty and twisted mind, taking pleasure in everyone else's suffering.

title: Ambition
summary: You despise being so weak and small, with no horns nor strength. You crave for the day you will be able to carve your place as rightful leader of a great herd.

title: Ambition: the guardian hears
summary: The little beast in your care is restless, violently trying to carve its place amongst the other children of age.

title: Lust
summary: Your natural inclination for violence has lately assumed a new flavour when you find yourself close to young people of the opposite gender, especially if...

title: Lust: the guardian hears
summary: The little beast in your care has developed an insatiable lust, abusing other children whenever manages to subdue them or, if nothing else is available,...

title: Horns grow
summary: A young male beastman grows horns, sized by his parents.

title: Horns lost in battle
summary: You try to fall back and the enemy's blade strikes true. When you come to your senses again, you realize only a couple of stumps remain where your horns used...

title: The herd attacks
summary: An AI beastman lord at peace attacks a civilised neighbour (beastman_migration CB).

title: A captive is taken
summary: on_siege_over_winner (random list).

title: The herd pillages
summary: A Chaos lord on a despoilment war takes a civilised capital: raze it, take captives, or pass through. on_siege_over_winner.

title: Our lands are pillaged
summary: The merciless herd of have wrought destruction and ruin in your lands, destroying any building they came across and hunting down people like monsters from...

title: The herd sacks a holding
summary: A beastman who wins a siege of a holding with four or more buildings can sack it for gold and learning (one building burnt, the holder and his top liege furious) or spare it for prestige. The province is then safe from another sack for ten years. Moved from the greenskin file (was WAAGH.9).

title: Captured slaves
summary: Sacrifice a slave at the herdstone, keep them, or let them go.

title: A prisoner is eaten
summary: The court is scared into submission. beastman_eat_prisoner.

title: Herdstone offering: a small horde
summary: Your offering has pleased the gods. A small host of Beastmen, lured in by the lure of trophies and blood, has decided to join your herd.

title: Herdstone offering: a large horde
summary: Your offering has pleased the gods. A large host of Beastmen, lured in by the promise of war and slaughter, has decided to join your herd.

title: Herdstone offering: giants
summary: Your offering has pleased the gods. A band of trolls and giants have wandered into your domain and have found a temporary home around your herdstone, joining...

title: Herdstone offering: raiders
summary: Raiders rise at the capital (beastmen.67).

title: Raiders rise
summary: A rebel warherd rises at the capital.

title: Raise a beastman retinue (elite)
summary: The herd has grown, and the mightiest beasts of the forest answer the call of the brayhorn. Which of them will march at your side?

title: Raise a beastman retinue
summary: Young gors gather at the herdstone, eager to prove themselves. Which of them will join your warherd?

title: Raise a Chaos retinue (elite)
summary: For Kurgan and Hung Chaos lords.

title: Raise a Chaos retinue
summary: For Kurgan and Hung Chaos lords.

title: The conquered rise
summary: A beastman lord holding civilised provinces faces a peasant revolt in one of them (beastmen.76).

title: Peasants rise
summary: Peasant rebels spawn and declare war on the top liege.

title: Lieges hear of the revolt
summary: The weak inhabitants have risen up in , led by a determined leader wanting to reclaim this land for their pitiable kind.

title: Too many clan titles
summary: Deactivates one of two clan titles held by a beastman ruler. Meant for on_inheritance but not hooked up (Komi, 2026-10-27: leave it unused).

title: Small but deadly
summary: A halfling with two daggers ambushes a beastman lord whose lands touch the Moot, or any beastman leading troops into the Moot or besieging a holding there. Fight (a martial gamble), bellow for the herd, or, for a bray shaman, curse the wretch. At most once every two years per character. by on_unit_entering_province and on_siege_pulse (random: beastmen_moot_ambush).

title: The Chaos moon
summary: Clears last year's full moon, or rolls for a new one: about once in 25 years, more often as the doom rises. Players hear of it (beastmen.86).

title: Morrslieb waxes
summary: The Chaos moon hangs full and green above the forest, and the herdstones hum. Every beast in the woods feels it: the hunger, the fury, the call of the Dark...

title: The shaman reads the signs
summary: Picks the omen and the shaman who reads it: a courtier, else a vassal, else the ruler.

title: The gods ask for blood
summary: Attack a civilised neighbour, or take the omen's fury into the next fight. Turning the gods down costs piety.

title: The herdstone sings
summary: The capital's herdstone hums with power. Gather the herd for a great rite, or feast.

title: Bad signs
summary: The entrails are black. The shaman asks for a sacrifice: a prisoner, gold, or nothing, and the herd's spirit sinks for two years.

title: The journey begins
summary: The pilgrim says farewell and sets off for the Heart of the Dark.

title: Planning the route
summary: Sets how many road events the journey has: two from near the Drakwald, three from further away, four from the far corners of the world. Distance is measured from Marienburg (province 222), at the edge of the forest.

title: Road event roll
summary: Picks one road event the pilgrim has not had yet. When the road events are used up, or none fits, the pilgrim reaches the Heart of the Dark (brayherd.4).

title: The Heart of the Dark
summary: The pilgrim arrives. Two events at the Heart of the Dark follow.

title: Smoke over the trees
summary: The warband stumbles on a human hamlet in the forest. Burn it, drag the survivors to the Herdstone as sacrifices (pleases the Herdstone most), or leave it and keep the pace.

title: A challenger in the warband
summary: A young gor of the pilgrim's own warband challenges for the leadership, as beastmen do. Fight him (better odds with martial skill, duelists and the brave), let the bestigors kill him (costs prestige), or, for the cunning, send him to lead a raid that goes wrong.

title: The Dark Omen
summary: Malagor, the crow-winged bray-shaman, reads the pilgrim's fate. Letting him read the entrails gives a good or ill omen (beastmen_blood_omen or beastmen_ill_omen); a sacrifice buys better odds; driving him off angers the Herdstone.

title: The Brass Bull
summary: Taurox, the Doombull of brass flesh, crashes past on an endless rampage. Join it (glory, wounds or worse; pleases the Herdstone), steer the minotaurs at a human town (cunning pilgrims), or get out of the way.

title: The drunken centigors
summary: A band of centigors, half-horse and wholly drunk, staggers into camp with stolen wine. Drink with them (they may ride along and boast of the pilgrim, or leave him with a habit), race their chief, or drive them off.

title: A warlord's invitation
summary: An AI beastman king or emperor (a rival if there is one) invites the pilgrim to his camp. Accept (brayherd.16), use it to murder a rival (schemers, brayherd.18) or keep to your own tent.

title: The warlord's feast
summary: Usually a good rest. A host who is not yet a friend may become one; a rival host may poison the pilgrim (eight times likelier if deceitful): half the time that kills, half the time it ends in brayherd.17.

title: Waking in a ditch
summary: The poisoned pilgrim survives with food poisoning (or poisoned, without Reapers) and a warning to stay away.

title: Fatal hospitality
summary: A schemer's murder attempt on the rival host: a clean kill and escape (more likely with high intrigue), a kill that costs the pilgrim's life, or a failure that does. Pilgrims who cannot die carry on with the journey.

title: A knight in the thorns
summary: The warband drags a knight of the man-things out of a thorn thicket, lost and alone. Save him for the Herdstone (the best offering), sell him back to his kin, or throw him in the fighting pit for sport.

title: Tracks of a Jabberslythe
summary: The pilgrim finds the work of a great Jabberslythe and can hunt it (brayherd.21). Hunters always do.

title: How the hunt goes
summary: Even odds: the pilgrim corners the beast (brayherd.23), meets a rival hunter (brayherd.22) or gets lost (brayherd.24).

title: The other hunter
summary: A lone bestigor hunts the same beast. Take him into your court (better odds at the kill), leave him be, or treat him as a rival (worse odds, and the pilgrim grows cruel and paranoid).

title: The Jabberslythe cornered
summary: Fighting gives prestige and a roll: mastery of the hunt, a wound, the beast escaping, maiming or death. A hunting companion makes mastery likelier, a slain rival maiming and death. Fleeing costs prestige and courage.

title: Lost in the forest
summary: The pilgrim wanders lost for weeks: may fall ill (if healthy), and may become stressed, depressed or wroth.

title: Heart of the Dark event roll
summary: Picks one event the pilgrim has not had yet at the Heart of the Dark. When they are used up, or none fits, the rite at the Herdstone follows (brayherd.39).

title: The fighting ring
summary: Bestigors brawl in a ring. Duelists win money and pride; others can try their luck. Fighting pleases the Herdstone; watching and betting does not.

title: The shrine of a single god
summary: Bestigors worship one Chaos god at a defiled altar. Joining in may make the pilgrim cynical or turn them to that god; an undivided pilgrim can denounce them (piety, but the Herdstone frowns); or study their symbols.

title: The herd market
summary: A market of meat, slaves and plunder. Feast (may turn gluttonous), buy a beastman artifact, or steal one (intrigue 15 or elusive shadow).

title: Before the Great Herdstone
summary: Ends the pilgrimage. The rite's outcome is rolled from the favour gathered on the journey plus half the pilgrim's diplomacy, rank and the Brayherd's opinion: a bad rite (favour 100 for those who humble themselves, at a cost in prestige), an okay one (favour 150) or a great one (favour 300, piety, martial and health).

title: A bray shaman for the court

title: The bray shaman arrives

title: A war leader for the court
summary: Boon: the governor sends a scarred bestigor of the ruler's god to lead the armies (strategist modifier, commander if a slot is free). Announced by brayherd.53.

title: The war leader arrives
summary: Letter from the governor; the bestigor becomes a commander if possible.

title: A daemonic artifact
summary: Boon: a random beastman artifact the ruler does not own yet.

title: A gift of Chaos
summary: Boon: a mutation (hides, runes, tusks, senses, limbs) or a bigger set of horns, up to a crown of horns. About one roll in six brings nothing visible. Every roll counts towards the mutation counter.

title: A request for a bray
summary: Boon: the governor picks a bride for a male ruler or relative, either from his own bloodline or a lowborn beauty, and gives her family, looks and a personality (abler while the Brayherd is united). Then brayherd.61. The decision only allows male grooms, so the bride is always created. FROMFROMFROM the groom.

title: The bride arrives
summary: The bride and groom can marry again; the wedding follows (brayherd.63).

title: A ruinous union
summary: The groom takes the bride as consort: prestige (more if she is of the Brayherd's own blood) and, for a ruler who married himself, five years of peace with the Brayherd. Tells the ruler who asked (brayherd.64).

title: The wedding is announced
summary: Tells the ruler who arranged a relative's wedding: 25 years of peace with the Brayherd.

title: The rage awakens
summary: A wrathful or aggressive warrior of the berserker peoples, young enough for the rage, or any open follower of Khorne, who becomes a berserker of Khorne. A coward is cured of it.

title: Maimed in the rage
summary: Shaking with the rage, you cleave the skull of yet another foe and turn to look for the next. Only then do you notice that your leg will not carry you: a spear...

title: Wounded in the rage
summary: Shaking with the rage, you cleave the skull of yet another foe and turn to look for the next. Only then do you notice the long arrow standing out of your...

title: Cut off and dragged down
summary: The berserker dies, slain by the enemy commander when there is one. The home liege (battle.11) and the enemy liege or commander (battle.14) hear of it, as for any fallen commander.

title: A swath through the enemy
summary: Your sight turns red and takes you. You charge without a thought for your own skin, and while your companions struggle to keep up, your axe cuts a wide swath...

title: The rage fades
summary: As old as a human of 50 (200 for a dwarf).

title: The rage rises
summary: A courtier who thinks little of the berserker drones on until the rage rises. The berserker fights it down, or not: patience and temperance help, wrath does not.

title: After the rage
summary: The courtier is beaten bloody and remembers it, or the table takes the blows and the gods see the berserker's will.

title: The call is made
summary: Ten years after a lord claimed the right to call a Black Crusade: if no war was declared, the claim lapses (bcrusade.2). decision in wh_chaos_decisions.txt, 3650 days later.

title: The claim lapses
summary: Hidden. A lord who holds the right to call a Black Crusade (title flag temp_religion_head) loses it again, unless he claimed it less than ten years ago, is preparing a Black Crusade or is fighting one. (wh_on_actions), by bcrusade.1, bcrusade.22 and the CBs when the war ends.

title: The cooldown begins
summary: Hidden. When a Black Crusade ends, that god may not call another for thirty years, or a hundred for a low-doom crusade. The timers are title flags on k_cult_of_sigmar. new_crusade CBs in 00_cb_types.

title: The cooldown ends
summary: Hidden. Clears Black Crusade timers older than thirty (or a hundred) years. can_call_black_crusade also treats such old timers as expired, so a Black Crusade can come again even with no Grand Theogonist.

title: Other lords are off limits
summary: Hidden. While a Black Crusade runs, every other independent ruler is flagged so the call CB does not show against them. on_crusade_monthly.

title: Lords are fair game again
summary: Hidden. Clears the flags bcrusade.5 set. CBs.

title: The chosen lord
summary: Hidden. Picks the official recipient of the target lands: the faithful holder, his heir, or a claimant the warlord likes. With nobody fit, pledged lords fall back to their own beneficiaries, and the horde is told by letter (bcrusade.130, .131). on_crusade_target_changes, and by bcrusade.11 and .12.

title: The chosen lord turns away
summary: Hidden. If the official recipient no longer follows the god of the crusade, a new one is picked (bcrusade.10).

title: The chosen lord dies
summary: Hidden. If the official recipient dies, a new one is picked (bcrusade.10).

title: Preparation begins
summary: Hidden. Tells every ruler of the faith that a Black Crusade is being prepared (bcrusade.14).

title: The faithful prepare for war
summary: The warlord asks for warriors against the target. A lord may pledge at once or wait.

title: The first pledges
summary: Hidden. AI rulers of the faith may pledge at the start, more often the zealous, the great and those whose lands lie in the target realm.

title: More pledges
summary: Hidden. While the horde is weaker than the defence, more AI lords are asked each month, the most zealous first.

title: An AI lord pledges
summary: Hidden. An AI lord pledges, adds to the war chest, and names a beneficiary for the lands: a kinsman with a claim, a child, another of his house, or nobody. CBs.

title: The Black Crusade marches
summary: Hidden. Announces the launch (bcrusade.19) and takes holy orders out of the war chest.

title: Black Crusade for the target
summary: The launch, seen by every ruler. The text says whether the target was once Chaos land (the Wastes, Norsca), on its fringe (the Darklands) or never held. Lords who promised the Forces of Order their help are called to the defence (bcrusade.25).

title: Called to the defence
summary: Hidden. A lord who promised to fight the Black Crusade joins the defender's wars, with an alliance and good opinion both ways.

title: No launch
summary: Hidden. The Black Crusade was cancelled: the faith is told (bcrusade.21) and its authority suffers.

title: The target turned
summary: The target secretly worshipped Chaos and has declared it; the horde must choose another.

title: The target falls to Chaos
summary: Hidden. If the target lands come into Chaos hands before the launch, the crusade is called off and its timers start (bcrusade.2, .3, .6).

title: Debts called in
summary: Hidden. The AI warlord makes an AI lord who owes him a favour pledge.

title: A debt called in
summary: Hidden. The warlord writes to a player who owes him a favour (bcrusade.32).

title: The warlord's letter
summary: A player who owes the warlord a favour is told to march.

title: Pledged
summary: Hidden. When a player pledges, one of bcrusade.41-45 may follow. on_pledge_crusade_participation.

title: A courtier approves
summary: A courtier is glad of the pledge.

title: Another lord approves
summary: Another pledged lord writes in approval; two zealots become friends.

title: A rival offers peace
summary: A rival marching in the same horde offers to end the feud.

title: The blood stirs
summary: The player feels the gods' call and becomes zealous.

title: A farewell to the old friend
summary: A mad lord says goodbye to the thing in the lake, or in the woods. supernatural events on.

title: Unpledged
summary: Hidden. When a player breaks the pledge, one of bcrusade.51-54 may follow.

title: A courtier is disgusted
summary: A courtier tells the player what they think of the broken pledge.

title: Another lord is displeased
summary: Another pledged lord writes in disgust.

title: A new rival
summary: Another pledged lord declares the player a rival.

title: Cast out
summary: Hidden. The warlord casts out the oath-breaker (trait excommunicated) and tells the faith (bcrusade.55).

title: Traitor to the gods
summary: The faith hears who broke the pledge.

title: The warlord writes
summary: Hidden. The warlord asks a player who has not pledged (bcrusade.61).

title: The warlord's summons
summary: Pledge, pay a year's income instead, or wait.

title: Beneficiaries checked
summary: Hidden. Each month, a beneficiary who died, got land, became an heir, a mercenary, a monk or too sick is dropped. AI lords pick a new one (bcrusade.17); players are told why (bcrusade.120). bcrusade.63). Fired from on_crusade_monthly and by bcrusade.63.

title: A beneficiary dies or is landed
summary: Hidden. Marks why, and has the warlord recheck (bcrusade.62).

title: The new lord of the conquered land
summary: A player may play on as the new ruler of the conquered realm. Fired by the new_crusade CB in 00_cb_types.

title: Pledges that no longer stand
summary: Hidden. Lords at war with the warlord, or no longer of the faith or landed, lose their pledge.

title: Taken back
summary: Hidden. A cast-out lord who pledges is forgiven by letter (bcrusade.67). .61, and by pledge_crusade_effect.

title: Forgiven
summary: The warlord lifts the curse on a lord who has come back to the horde.

title: The beneficiary's new land
summary: Hidden. Prepares bcrusade.71.

title: The lord in the conquered land
summary: A player whose beneficiary got a county in the conquered realm may play on as the beneficiary.

title: Defence pledges
summary: Hidden. Rulers of the target's faith, and Old World, Dawi, Ormazd, halfling and Cathay rulers when the target is one of them, may pledge to the defence (bcrusade.81). More do so near the target, when doom is high, or when the Everchosen walks. by bcrusade.82.

title: A defence pledge
summary: Hidden. A ruler of the target's faith pledges to the defence; other faiths promise to join when the horde marches (flag forces_of_order_defender, used by bcrusade.19). Kings and emperors write to the target (bcrusade.85).

title: A new target
summary: Hidden. If the target changes to a ruler of another faith, defence pledges are sought again (bcrusade.80).

title: The defence is outmatched
summary: Hidden. When the horde is far stronger, more of the target's faith come to help.

title: Debts to the defender
summary: Hidden. An AI ruler who owes the target a favour pledges to the defence.

title: A promise of help
summary: The target hears that a king of the faith will stand by them.

title: The first offerings
summary: Hidden. The warlord puts half his treasury, piety, prestige and four artifacts in the war chest.

title: Gold for the war
summary: Hidden. AI rulers of the faith who do not march are asked to pay (bcrusade.92).

title: A gift of gold
summary: Hidden. An AI ruler gives a year's income or more, by zeal.

title: Gold for the marchers
summary: Hidden. A fifth of the war chest's gold goes out at the launch.

title: A siege won
summary: Hidden. Each siege won by the horde fills the war chest.

title: A battle won
summary: Hidden. Each battle won by the horde fills the war chest. hooks.

title: No spoils for holy orders
summary: Hidden. Holy orders get no share of the war chest.

title: A new master
summary: Hidden. When an order gets a new master, bcrusade.96 runs again.

title: A gift to the war chest
summary: A lord gives one, two or four years of income for piety. donate decision).

title: A fellow warlord's camp
summary: A player passes the camp of another lord sworn to the Black Crusade, who invites him to share his fire.

title: Strange lands
summary: The commander spends some days among a foreign people. He can study them, befriend one of them, shut them out, or, once he knows them well and is of a kindred race, take up their ways.

title: The field of the dead
summary: The host crosses an old battlefield. The commander can bury his own, bury everyone, take trophies for the gods, or rob the dead.

title: The merchant caravan

The piece depends on the faith of the land (wh_black_crusade_effects.txt). Rare: once a lifetime, and only if the commander has not bought from one before.

title: Far from home
summary: The long march weighs on the commander. He presses on, eases off, or leans on his god.

title: The twin-tailed comet
summary: A comet crosses the night sky and the camp reads it as a sign. Seen twice, a sign and a firm hand together make the commander hear a voice of battle.

title: Heads on the road
summary: Some of the host behead locals for their faith. The commander joins in, condemns it, or calls it a needed lesson.

title: The hidden faithful
summary: Deep in enemy land, a few locals of the commander's own faith take the host in. He can pay to spread the faith there, take one of them home, or just thank them.

title: The cutpurse
summary: A street boy steals the commander's purse. He laughs it off, hunts the boy down, or takes him into service.

title: The hedge sorcerer
summary: The commander visits a local sorcerer. He learns from him, or kills him and takes his books. Khornates lose zeal for it; mages gain magic experience; the gifted may wake to a lore.

title: The old festival
summary: The host comes upon a festival to old gods. The commander joins in, keeps apart, or loses himself in it.

title: A voice in the night
summary: After a long night of drink, the commander hears his god tell him to give all to the war. He obeys, blames the wine, or, if he is zealous and holy enough, gives up his lands to take the vows of a holy order of his faith.

title: Riders of the order
summary: Knights of a holy order of the commander's faith share his camp, and their master asks him to sit up and talk. A friend, or an insult.

title: The tavern
summary: A serving girl or boy in a tavern takes an interest in the commander. He sends them off, takes one night, or brings them home as a lover.

title: The men are restless
summary: A long halt sours the host. The commander drills them or fires them up; done twice over each, he becomes a great general.

title: The prophet of doom

title: The Penitent Host

summary: Narrative for every player: the host won, and its prophet is a king. shepherds_crusade_invasion CB (on_success_title).

title: The prophet is dead
summary: Narrative for every player: the prophet fell and the host scatters. shepherds_crusade_invasion CB (on_attacker_leader_death).

title: Writing a book
summary: The lord picks a topic: war, diplomacy and intrigue, rule, faith or the dynasty, as education and skills allow (one at random may be out of mind this time). Progress events follow (book.2 - 5) and the book is done in 1.5 to 11 years (book.10).

title: Scribes and ink
summary: The work needs more scribes, ink and time: pay, help (a learned or mad writer does better, a dull one worse), or rush.

title: Unhappy with the work
summary: The writer doubts the book and may ask a fitting councillor, spouse or lover for advice, or press on stressed.

title: Writer's block
summary: The writer is stuck: a walk that may end in a fall, a strange drink the court physician brews, or rest.

title: Up all night
summary: Inspiration strikes at night; the writer may stay up working, at a risk to health.

title: The book is finished
summary: The book is done: its quality follows the potential set by the topic, the progress events and the writer's stats and traits, and a title is chosen from many, some named for a spouse, lover, rival, ancestor or saint. Great poets may find a calling.

title: General Winter
summary: Hidden. A foreign commander marches into a Kislevite province in winter, at war with its lord: the province turns hostile with cold (supply and attrition) for three months, and he may fall ill. Kislevites, the peoples of the Wastes and Norsca, the dead and daemons do not feel it.

title: Call the Winter
summary: An Ice Witch calls an early winter on the enemies in her lord's Kislevite lands (decision bulwark_call_winter). The besieged and occupied provinces freeze for half a year. One time in three the cold comes home too: a famine at her lord's capital.

title: The Spring Driving comes
summary: Hidden. Picks the chieftain: the lord's old nemesis if he still lives, otherwise a new one from a Kurgan court (or a Chaos court of the Wastes).

title: The Spring Driving
summary: The chieftain's riders come over the river into the lord's lands. Ride out to meet them (a fight, and a chance to kill him), hold the stanitsa walls (a Frost Ward helps; if it holds it becomes a Stanitsa of Heroes), or pay them to ride on. A burned stanitsa sends refugees south (bulwark.12). event_target:spring_province the province raided.

title: Refugees from the north
summary: The burned stanitsa's people come south with what they could carry. Settle them in the lord's capital (more hands and taxes, more unrest), or turn them away.

title: The chieftain falls
summary: The lord cuts down the chieftain who led the Spring Driving. His skull-torc can be taken, once in a lifetime, and the Wastes are a little weaker.

title: The Motherland Calls
summary: Hidden. A Black Crusade falls on a Kislevite realm: its ruler and every Kislevite lord of the realm take heart (morale, levy reinforcement, less revolt) until the war ends. The first time the Tsardom itself is the target, the Oath of Karaz brings the Dwarfs (bulwark.25).

title: The Motherland Calls
summary: Notice for the ruler under the Black Crusade.

title: The Crusade is broken
summary: The Black Crusade against Kislev has failed. Great prestige, and the doom of the world falls back.

title: The Crusade ends
summary: Hidden. The war with the Black Crusade ended in its victory or a white peace: the Motherland Calls ends.

title: The Oath of Karaz
summary: The first time a Black Crusade falls on the Tsardom, the Dwarfs of the World's Edge keep the old oath for the passes near Praag: a Dwarf captain and a small host come to the Tzar(ina) until the peace.

title: The Siege of Praag
summary: Hidden. A Chaos army has Praag under siege. Praag's lord is asked about a sortie (bulwark.31); the breach comes a month later (bulwark.32), and if Praag still stands in half a year it holds (bulwark.34).

title: A sortie from Praag
summary: The hordes are at the walls of Praag. Lead a sortie out of the north gate (glory or wounds), or keep the walls.

title: The breach
summary: The wall is down by the north gate. A hero of the court holds the breach to the last (bulwark.33), or the lord fights there himself.

title: The last stand at the breach
summary: The hero holds the breach until the wall is shored up behind him, and dies there. Praag sings of him.

title: Praag holds
summary: Half a year after the Chaos siege began, Praag is still in the hands of its lord and free of the siege. Great prestige, and a cut to doom.

title: A great city falls
summary: Hidden. A Chaos army takes Kislev, Praag or Erengrad: the doom of the world rises (minor; medium for Kislev itself).

title: Chaos crosses the Lynsk
summary: Hidden. A Chaos commander enters the Lynsk lands at war with the ruler of the Tsardom, who must choose how to meet him (bulwark.41).

title: The Lynsk Line
summary: The hordes are across the Lynsk. Hold the river (its forts stand stronger, but the levies bleed), or pull back to the cities, burn the land behind you and raise a fresh host (bulwark.42).

title: A fresh host
summary: Half a year after the pull-back, a fresh host is ready at the capital.

title: A stanitsa under siege
summary: Hidden. A Chaos army besieges a holding in northern Kislev whose lord is a Kislevite count with a liege. The liege must answer (bulwark.46).

title: The Last Stand of the Stanitsa
summary: A small garrison in the north is holding against a whole horde to buy the realm time. Ride to relieve it (glory or wounds, and its lord's love), or let it fall (the time it bought strengthens the realm; its lord does not forget). event_target:stand_province the province.

title: Dwarf rangers
summary: Rangers from the World's Edge come down to fight: a small elite company.

title: Volunteers from the Empire
summary: A free company of Ostland and Talabecland men crosses the border to fight.

title: The Gryphon Legion rides home
summary: The Legion comes back from the Empire to fight for Kislev, for free.

title: A wandering Grail Knight
summary: A Grail Knight of Bretonnia who heard of the war rides in and offers his lance. He joins the court.

title: An Ice Witch coven
summary: A coven of Ice Witches freezes the camps of the enemy in the realm's Kislevite lands.

title: Ursun's bears
summary: Wild bears come out of the woods at night and fall on the Chaos camp. The enemy's commanders may be mauled.

title: The White Wolf company
summary: The Knights of the White Star ride from Erengrad to fight beside the realm. They are Ulricans, and the priests of Ursun do not like it.

title: A High Elf mage
summary: An Asur mage who came on the Erengrad ships offers to stand with the realm for the war: he joins the court, and his magic breaks the enemy's nerve. Erengrad.

title: The Strigany warn of a night raid
summary: Strigany travellers bring word of a night attack, and the realm's armies are ready for it. A small favour is owed.

title: The Tzar's Call
summary: Envoys from Kislev (decision bulwark_tzars_call) ask a power of order for help against Chaos. Join the war, send a host under a captain of your own, send gold, or refuse. The AI weighs opinion, distance, its own wars, faith, doom, and old debts. Helpers win the Shield of the North (Kislev's opinion for thirty years) and prestige.

title: An answer to the Call
summary: Notice: a power has answered the Call with men or gold.

title: Brothers in the North
summary: The ruler of Kislev offers the Emperor the old treaty (decision bulwark_brothers_in_the_north): an alliance between the two crowns. Accept or refuse.

title: The brothers are sworn
summary: Notice: the Emperor has sworn the treaty.

title: The Emperor's call
summary: The Empire faces Chaos and the Emperor calls on Kislev (decision bulwark_emperors_call). Old debts make refusal costly.

title: A champion of Chaos slain
summary: Hidden. A Kislevite ruler or a member of the Circle of the Bear kills a Chaos champion, chosen or daemon prince: the doom of the world falls back a little, and the killer hears of it (bulwark.81).

title: The champion is dead
summary: is dead, and you killed him. One less champion of the Ruinous Powers walks the world. The priests of Ursun will hear of it before nightfall.

title: The Gate holds
summary: Once a decade, if Kislev, Praag and Erengrad are all held by Kislev's gods, the wall stands and doom falls back a little.

title: The Tzar falls to Chaos
summary: Hidden. The ruler of Kislev is killed by a follower of Chaos: the doom of the world rises, and a great boyar claims the crown.

title: A bear of Urskin's blood
summary: The Tzar's bear-master brings out a great bear of the line of Urskin, the bear that Tzar Boris rode. One per Tzar: it serves its rider and dies with him, or goes back to the wilds (kislevnorth.2).

title: Hidden. The rider of Urskin's bear dies: the bear lies down
summary: on his grave and dies too, or goes back into the forests around Kislev (a province modifier there for ten years). It never passes to an heir.

title: The caravan from the east
summary: A caravan comes down the High Pass from Cathay with jade, silk, spices and ivory. Escort it (gold, a chance of raiders, kislevnorth.11), tax it hard (more gold, a chance that Cathay's merchants shun the road, kislevnorth.12), or let it pass freely (Praag's trade grows for five years).

title: Raiders on the Pass
summary: Ogres or greenskins fall on the caravan in the Pass. Ride to its rescue (martial: loot and prestige, or the escort fee lost), or let them have it.

title: Cathay shuns the Pass
summary: Word of the Praag tolls has reached the merchants of Cathay, and the caravans go round by the south for ten years. No caravan comes in that time, and Praag's trade suffers.

title: The Kreml Guard swears
summary: The captain of the Kreml Guard kneels before the Tzar(ina) and swears the guard's oath in person. For as long as they reign the guard protects them against knives in the dark. Comes when the guard is founded and with each new holder of the crown.

title: The Kossars come home
summary: Ten years after the company was hired out to a southern prince, the Kossars come home: veterans who make the levies better, gold from the south, or a long list of the dead.

title: A letter from the Kossars
summary: The Kossar captain writes from the south: a siege in Tilea, a battle in the Border Princes, a prince who is slow to pay.

title: Longships on the coast
summary: Norscan longships come in to the coast to raid. Fight them on the shore (martial; a captured jarl, kislevnorth.41, or a burned coast), pay them off, or ambush them at sea with Erengrad's ships.

title: The captured jarl
summary: The raiders are broken and their jarl is in chains. Ransom him to his people (gold), bring him to Ursun (he joins the court on Kislev's faith), or keep him as a hostage (no Norscan raids on this coast for ten years).

title: Trolls in the thaw
summary: In the far north the trolls come down with the thaw. Hunt it (martial; a rare troll-hide cloak, once a lifetime; or a wound, and the troll heals and comes back, kislevnorth.51), pay troll-hunters, or bar the gates.

title: The troll comes back
summary: The troll that was cut down a year ago has grown its arm back and is eating the herds again. Burn it this time, or call on the Circle of the Bear.

title: Hidden. Kislev builds tall
summary: Once an AI Tzar(ina) holds all of Kislev's de jure lands, the crown turns from conquest to defence: a hidden trait lowers ambition and raises zeal, so the AI weakens Chaos and the beasts on its borders and builds at home rather than marching on its neighbours. Removed again if the realm loses de jure land.

summary: The steward takes the plan to the ruler (business.12).

title: A merchant ship

summary: They pay part of the cost. Word of the venture may reach a merchant prince nearby (business.17). A failed theft ends it here (business.20).

title: The view from the top
summary: Nine times in ten the priest goes over the edge (business.51); once in ten the ruler does (business.50).

title: The priest bends down
summary: I put all my weight behind my outstretched arms to push off the tower, and just then bends down. must have spotted a coin. I stumble past and out into the...

title: The priest falls
summary: As admires the view from the top of the tower, I reach out and give a gentle push.

title: The tower is finished
summary: The builder becomes an architect (or keeps it a pastime for more prestige). Five times in a hundred the tower will begin to lean in ten years (three times that for a boy's work).

title: The tower leans
summary: Its builder may blame the mason (imprisoned), the workers or themselves; a later holder can only shrug. Then: save it (business.54).

title: Saving the tower
summary: More coin, better odds.

title: The tower stands, crooked
summary: Three years later a famous visitor comes to see it (business.57).

title: The tower falls
summary: I wake in the middle of the night to a great crack, then a long rumbling like the loudest thunder I have ever heard. I rush to the window, fearing the worst,...

title: A visitor from afar
summary: A famous foreign statesman wants to meet the genius behind the leaning tower. The tower becomes a wonder that draws coin (leaning_tower). A blamed mason is released, and a boy mason may be lured away with a county of his own by a foreign ruler.

title: A garden gone wild
summary: Greeting the sun from my window one morning, I notice for the first time how the castle garden has been left to rot for years. The weeds are knee-high and the...

title: The weeds
summary: Clearing the weeds from a garden this size is hard work. It will take many days of toil before the hedges for the maze can even be planted.

title: Statues for the dead ends
summary: Of the family, of the gods and heroes of the faith (not for the faiths that forbid images), or none.

title: A fountain
summary: Plain, or flowing with wine (with ale for a Dawi), or none. A vampire may fill it with blood (a hidden one risks discovery, business.67), a Tomb King with the sacred waters of the Vitae, a daemon with the raw stuff of the Realm of Chaos.

title: Flowers
summary: It is time to fill the beds round the garden. I could bring in rare blooms from far away, from the gardens of Tilea and the hothouses of Marienburg, or plant...

title: A pavilion
summary: There is an unused spot in a quiet corner of the garden. Some would say it is the perfect place for a cosy pavilion.

title: The maze is finished
summary: Three of the four extras make it a magnificent maze. The gardener's calling, or a pastime.

title: Whispers by the fountain
summary: A hidden vampire's fountain of blood is seen for what it is.

title: The carpenters' guild
summary: A group of carpenters in have begun working together and taking on apprentices of their own. This cannot be ignored. I can approve their guild and win the good...

title: New coin for the realm
summary: True coin for glory, or debased coin for profit (which may be found out, business.72). Once every two years.

title: The coin is found out
summary: A merchant has found that my new coins are debased, with far less silver in them than they should hold. The whole realm is calling me a cheat and a skinflint.

title: A burgher wants land
summary: asks to buy a plot of my land in . It is a hard choice, for offers to pay well for it.

title: A workshop to fund
summary: Two years later it thrives (business.75) or goes under (business.76).

title: The workshop thrives
summary: The craftsmen I backed two years ago have come to tell me of their success. With my coin they set up their workshop, and it is now one of the most profitable...

title: The workshop goes under
summary: There is a faint knock at my door, and a small figure peeks in. I remember him well: one of the craftsmen I backed two years ago. Shamefaced, he tells me that...

title: A head for business
summary: Ever since I took up the pursuit of wealth and began to keep a close eye on income and spending, my coffers have been full more often than not.

title: The Carnival takes to the road
summary: Hidden. Picks a rural town in the ruler's lands, creates the Carnival Master (a secret sorcerer of Nurgle in a fine mask) and his troupe (a Tainted One and a Brute, Nurglite humans) and sends the arrival. More likely when the doom is high and for players. carnival_of_chaos.

title: Painted wagons
summary: The Carnival stops outside a town of the ruler's and promises a play. Welcome them, have them watched, turn them away or arrest the lot. The text changes with the land: an Empire burgher fair, a Tilean commedia troupe, an Estalian fiesta, Bretonnian mummers or Kislevite wandering players.

title: Empty cells
summary: The arrested players die in the night of a bloating sickness, the gaolers sicken, and the painted wagon and its Master are gone. The Carnival moves on.

title: The omens begin
summary: Hidden. Sends one omen the host has not had yet (carnival.11-14). After two omens the play comes (carnival.20). If the truth was seen, the camp can be raided before the show (carnival.25).

title: Sour milk
summary: The milk sours in the pail, the butter will not come and the dogs howl all night at the wagons. Look into it or let it be. A Strigany realm can blame the Strigany instead: easy, and wrong.

title: Flies, flies
summary: A child of the town wakes screaming from a dream of a fat, laughing grandfather, saying "Flies, flies, eat up his eyes!". Then other children have the same dream.

title: The jester's touch
summary: The watcher saw a jester take a girl's hand while he joked with her. By morning she has a weeping sore. Look into it, or burn the sore out and say nothing.

title: The Dance of Death
summary: At dusk a line of townsfolk dances behind the piper, three times round the town, laughing. Not all of them come home. (White Dwarf 119: the night before the attack, three circuits round the village.)

title: What the watcher found
summary: The watcher reports. A seer (witch hunter, wizard, Ice Witch, Grail Knight, Damsel), a sharp spymaster or a sharp ruler may see through the paint: then the camp can be raided before the show. Otherwise nothing is found.

title: The play
summary: The big night: a crude, funny, filthy piece that mocks the ruler. The play changes with the land (The Emperor's True Face, Orfeo and Pustulate, A Midsummer Nightmare, Papa Noigul's Festering Children). Laugh along (the jesters' touch may infect the court), walk out, look closer, or watch the Master instead of the stage. Sunset follows (carnival.30).

title: Grandfather's gift
summary: Between the acts the Master comes to the ruler's seat and offers a gift from Grandfather Nurgle: the patron's bond (a secret fall to Nurgle, doom up, once in a life a Plague Cart). Refuse him, or seize him before sunset.

title: Where shall we play next
summary: The new patron chooses where the Carnival goes next: a rival, an enemy, or wherever the road leads. The town is spared, and the Carnival leaves.

title: Before the show
summary: The truth was seen in time. Burn the wagons at dawn (the Master flees), storm the camp with the guard, or call in the witch hunters. Ice Witches, Grail Knights and paid Tilean blades give their own options.

title: Sunset
summary: The paint runs and the costumes split: Plaguebearers chanting their count, Nurglings spilling from the Plague Cart, the Tainted laughing. Fight (better if forewarned), fire the wagons, flee and seal the town, or bargain with the Master. The Master shows his true faith.

title: The square is held
summary: The daemons are driven back into the Cart and the Brethren cut down. The Master flees with the last wagons: the hunt can begin (carnival.40).

title: The town is lost
summary: The square is lost, or the gates were sealed on the living. The plague takes the town, women and children of the court are led away with a finger missing, and the Carnival moves on.

title: The Master ascends
summary: Rare and once per game (carnival.30 rolls it; only on a lost sunset). On the bodies of the town the Master is raised to a Daemon Prince of Nurgle and forges a small realm: the town's county and up to two of its neighbours break away under him, with a daemon host to hold them. His troupe stays at his court. The doom rises, the host keeps claims on the lost counties, and the Carnival is over.

title: The Master taken
summary: The Master is in chains, or dead in the dust. Burn him (doom falls, the Master's mask may be taken), or give him to the witch hunters (piety). Ends the Carnival.

title: The Master flees
summary: The Master is gone with the last wagons. Hunt him across the land, or let him go to plague someone else.

title: One town behind
summary: Up to three steps of the chase, always a town behind: an emptied village, a field of fingers, a child singing the Master's song. Press on (a roll that may corner him, carnival.42) or give up.

title: The Plague Cart
summary: The Master is cornered at the Cart, chalking the pentagram that opens onto Grandfather's garden. Face him yourself, or send the guard.

title: The Carnival moves on
summary: Hidden. Clears the old host's flags and sends the Carnival to the next realm: the patron's choice if there is one, else a lord two provinces away. After three realms, or if the Master is dead or taken, or no host is found, it ends (carnival.90).

title: The Carnival has gone
summary: Word reaches the old host that the painted wagons are now in another lord's lands.

title: The Carnival vanishes
summary: Hidden. Ends the chain: a living, free Master walks off the map, the global flag and targets are cleared, and a new Carnival may start in some later decade.

title: The Carnival plays for your enemy
summary: Word to a player patron that the Carnival has reached the next realm.

title: A death on the road
summary: Hidden. If the Master dies, the chain ends a month later (carnival.90 on the host). If the host dies while the Carnival is in their lands, the Master moves on (carnival.80 from the Master).

title: The road goes quiet
summary: Hidden. Five years after the Carnival reached a realm, if it has not moved since (a step that could not fire), it ends.

title: An invitation to a feast
summary: The invitee accepts (carousing.2), declines (carousing.3) or, as a zealot of a strict faith of Araby, declines and condemns the host's decadence (carousing.4). The AI weighs its traits, health, wars and its liege.

title: A guest accepts
summary: The guest gains the opinion_carousing modifier that marks them as a guest.

title: A guest declines
summary: Dear ,Unfortunately I cannot join you for merrymaking at this time. Thank you for your kind invitation.Until next time,

title: A zealot condemns the feast
summary: Dear ,It saddens me that you have become such a decadent wretch. Surely laughs at your excesses, but I, for one, will have no part in them. Wine is the first...

title: The day of the feast
summary: Hidden. Four months after the first invitation: no guest cancels (carousing.13), war or incapacity cancels (carousing.11), otherwise the party starts (carousing.14).

title: The feast is cancelled
summary: War or illness: the host frees the guests (carousing.12).

title: Word of the cancellation
summary: Dear ,Unfortunate circumstances force me to cancel the feast we had planned. We will make up for it when times are happier.Until then,

title: Nobody came
summary: No one accepted my invitation. One person makes no feast, so it will have to wait for another day.

title: Let the feast begin
summary: The host and every guest (carousing.15) carouse for forty days. Something happens on day fifteen (carousing.16); the party ends on day thirty (carousing.60). Half the gatherings of a Slaaneshi host are orgies (flag party_orgy), and the orgy takes the place of the day-fifteen happening.

title: A guest arrives
summary: I have arrived at the private rooms of . There is food and drink in plenty, and the mood is decidedly merry. I am looking forward to this!
