title: What happens at the feast
summary: Hidden. A Slaaneshi orgy (flag party_orgy) has its orgy (carousing.70). Otherwise picks one happening by the traits of the host and guests: the cannibal (a madman or a cannibal, and an AI at the table, 20), the fling (both lustful, 25), a new friend (30), a brawl (35), the lunatic (40), the drunkard (45) or the game (50). Unliving hosts often have their own night instead: a vampire's night court (65), a Tomb King's feast of the dead (67) or a daemon's revel (69).

title: Who is hungry?
summary: Hidden. A mad, possessed or impaling host (or one who owns the Omnivore) is tempted (carousing.21); otherwise such a guest is, but only at an AI host's table.

title: A sleeping guest
summary: Leave them be (a fright: craven, stressed, depressed), or eat: the host eats a guest, a guest eats the host. Either way the eater becomes a cannibal.

title: Who makes the first move?
summary: Hidden. The host, or a lustful guest who suits the host, makes the advance (carousing.26).

title: The attraction grows
summary: Propose (to a suitable guest, or to the host: carousing.27) or hold back (the lustful may grow stressed or depressed; others chaste).

title: A whispered proposal
summary: Accept (good times, a chance of a child or disease, carousing.28) or refuse (spurned, perhaps chaste, carousing.29).

title: A night to remember
summary: welcomed my advances, and we spent the rest of the night together, enjoying each other...

title: Spurned
summary: declined my amorous advances. I excuse myself and return to the pleasures of the table. Soon the embarrassing moment is forgotten... almost.

title: Friends in drink
summary: The host befriends a guest who is neither friend nor rival yet; the guest hears of it (carousing.31).

title: A new friend
summary: These days of revelry are a fine escape. So many laughs and so many heartfelt conversations in so short a time... It brings me closer to my companions, and I...

title: Who throws the first punch?
summary: Hidden. A wrathful, mad or paranoid host or guest flies into a rage (carousing.36).

title: Someone has to pay!
summary: The brawler goes for a guest (or the host); the target answers (carousing.37).

title: Fists up
summary: Fight back (beaten, wounded or rarely maimed; perhaps rivals), talk them down (diplomacy 15: perhaps friends and a point of diplomacy), or run (perhaps craven, no longer brave). The brawler learns how it went (carousing.38).

title: After the brawl
summary: The brawler is hurt too after a fight (perhaps called the Quarreller), reconciled after talk, or wary of a target who ran.

title: Who goes wild?
summary: Hidden. A mad host or guest steals the show (carousing.41).

title: This party needs some action!
summary: The madman has the time of their life (perhaps called the Merry), and the others approve (carousing.42).

title: Laughing too hard to stand
summary: is feasting and revelling like a madman. I can hardly stand up, I am laughing so hard.

title: Who drinks too much?
summary: Hidden. A drunkard host or guest overdoes it (carousing.46).

title: I can handle it
summary: An epic hangover (perhaps called the Drunkard). Fellow drunkards respect it, the others despise it (carousing.47).

title: A champion, or a disgrace
summary: is clearly going overboard with drinking.

title: Bounce to the host
summary: Hidden, so the guest is FROM in carousing.51.

title: Out comes the board
summary: The host plays the guest for money or for honour (carousing.52).

title: The game is set
summary: The guest plays; the cleverer player is three times as likely to win. Both learn the result (carousing.53).

title: The last move
summary: The winner takes 5 gold if they played for money and may become an apprentice boardgamer; the loser pays.

title: The morning after
summary: Host and guests go home: prestige, perhaps relief from stress or depression, and a party timer. A host on the carousing focus becomes a carouser, then a dedicated carouser, and may then turn hedonist or socializer (never hedonist for a Tomb King, nor for a daemon not of Slaanesh); a player who won at the board may become a gamer.

title: The host has died
summary: Hidden. Frees the guests of a host who dies before the feast.

title: The night court
summary: A vampire host and a living guest, flushed with wine, alone in an alcove. A taste, a deep draught (the guest dies), or nothing. A hidden vampire risks being seen (carousing.66).

title: Seen
summary: Someone saw what the host did in the alcove.

title: The feast of the dead
summary: The dead do not eat. A Tomb King keeps the old rites of offering, lets the living guests enjoy the food, or sets a skeleton behind every chair.

title: The revel of the Neverborn
summary: A daemon's feast leaves a mortal guest changed: let the Warp take their mind, take their soul for the gods, or send them home whole to spread the tale.

title: The revel of the Prince
summary: A Slaaneshi host's orgy. The host leads the rites (piety, and a guest of matching tastes in the host's bed) or watches from the dais (prestige). Every guest then chooses (carousing.71).

title: The orgy
summary: A guest joins the revel (good times, perhaps the host's bed, a little of Slaanesh's favour, and for the lustful of other faiths a taste for more) or slips away (a zealous guest of another faith is disgusted with the host).

title: An envoy of Cathay comes to trade
summary: Hidden. Rarely, and once in a lord's life, a Cathayan envoy of the Celestial Court comes to trade treasures; one time in ten a famed strategist. Less likely in hard times or if a treasure of Cathay is held, likelier in a golden age or an expansionist reign.

title: The envoy is announced
summary: Hidden. The envoy presents themselves to the lord (cathayart.3).

title: An envoy of Cathay
summary: The envoy offers a treasure for a eunuch, a concubine or gold, or for a feast; refusing sends the envoy home and costs a little grace. The Emperor's likes and dislikes weigh on the treasure (cathayart.4).

title: The treasure of the envoy
summary: A treasure of Cathay the lord does not hold yet, better if the Emperor liked the trade; a bad feast gets nothing but lost grace. The envoy then goes home.

title: A councillor's parting gift
summary: A Cathayan guest leaves a treasure of Cathay, likelier the Art of War for a lord of martial skill whose guest was a marshal.

title: An imperial spouse dies
summary: Hidden. When a prince or princess of Cathay dies after five years at a western court, unmurdered by their liege, Cathay may send its condolences: a letter, a treasure the dead loved, or the mourner finds their journal (cathayart.11). Not while Cathay is isolationist.

title: The condolences arrive
summary: Hidden. If the Viceroy still has the keepsake, the mourner gets the letter (cathayart.12), the treasure (cathayart.13) or the journal (cathayart.14); else the letter.

title: A letter of condolence
summary: The mourner may read the letter, for grace and a risk of grief, or set it aside, perhaps healing from grief.

title: A keepsake from Cathay
summary: The Viceroy sends the treasure the dead loved; taking it risks grief, refusing may heal it.

title: The journal
summary: The mourner finds the journal of the dead and may keep it, or burn it and turn cynical.

title: A councillor sets out
summary: Hidden. One of the Jade Viceroy's Cathayan councillors picks a reason to visit a ruler at peace with the Viceroy: talks for the chancellor, the troops or military study for the marshal, taxes or trade for the steward, preaching or philosophy for the priest (the first of each pair for a tributary). Likelier in a golden age, under an expansionist policy, with a tributary and with more grace; rarer while Cathay suffers, and rare without grace.

title: The councillor writes ahead
summary: Hidden. Saves the guest and remembers the host, so that the guest's death or jailing can be answered (celestial.18), and sends the host the letter (celestial.3).

title: A letter from the Jade Viceroy's court
summary: The councillor asks to visit. Welcoming the guest wins a little grace; the visit comes in about two months (celestial.4), and the host is cleared for new guests a while after (celestial.20). Turning the guest away costs much grace and offends the councillor and the Viceroy.

title: The visit
summary: Hidden. The guest arrives. If the host's own councillor for the same office is skilled, all goes well (celestial.5); otherwise the omen of falling stars (celestial.6), the greeting in Grand Cathay's tongue (celestial.7), the borrowed silks (celestial.12) or the talk about the weather (celestial.13). The tongue and the silks need a host of another culture than the guest.

title: A visit well kept
summary: The host's councillor prepared everything, and the guest goes home pleased with a minor gain of grace. One time in ten the guest leaves a Cathayan treasure (cathayart.5), once per life and only if none is held.

title: Falling stars
summary: Shooting stars cross the sky as host and guest watch the moons, and the guest leaves at once, sure the visit is cursed: a minor loss of grace. A Cathayan host laughs it off with the guest.

title: Words in the Emperor's tongue
summary: The night before the audience, the host may spend all night learning the greeting (a learned host succeeds more often and gains grace and a step towards Multilingual, celestial.8; otherwise oversleeps, celestial.9), an hour or two (celestial.10 or the stumble, celestial.11), or leave it to the translator. A host who already speaks the tongue greets the guest flawlessly.

title: Flawless
summary: The host learned the tongue and greeted the guest flawlessly: a major gain of grace and Student of Language, or Multilingual for a former student. Rarely (15%) the guest leaves a Cathayan treasure (cathayart.5), once per life and only if none is held.

title: Asleep in the library
summary: The host fell asleep over the phrasebook and missed the audience: a major loss of grace.

title: Well said
summary: A simple greeting, well enough spoken: a medium gain of grace, and one time in ten a Cathayan treasure (cathayart.5), once per life and only if none is held.

title: A stumble
summary: The host forgot every other word: a minor loss of grace.

title: Borrowed silks
summary: The host greeted the guest in Cathayan silks bought from a merchant, with marks only the Dragon Emperor's family may wear: a minor loss of grace. The host may punish the merchant (a little gold back, a little cruelty).

title: Talk about the weather
summary: Small talk in the garden about the clear sky is taken as a fine compliment to the Dragon Emperor, the Son of Heaven: a medium gain of grace, and rarely (15%) a Cathayan treasure (cathayart.5), once per life and only if none is held. A Cathayan host simply enjoys the talk.

title: The guest is lost
summary: Hidden. A councillor on a visit died or was jailed: the host hears of it (celestial.19), unless the councillor died going home to Cathay, and is cleared for new guests (celestial.20).

title: An awkward letter
summary: The host must tell the Jade Viceroy that the guest died, vanished or sits in a cell. An apology with a gift (50 prestige and 15 gold, which go to Cathay) or silence.

title: Clean-up
summary: Hidden. Clears the visit flags of the host and the guest, so that the host can receive a new guest. celestial.18) or FROMFROM (from celestial.19).

title: Complaints from the caravans
summary: Hidden. A ruler with a trade post on a road to Grand Cathay (the Ivory Road, the Old Silk Road, the Khyprian Road or the Spice Route) and a vassal with a city hears from the Jade Viceroy (celestial.31).

title: The Viceroy writes
summary: Hidden. Sends the letter (celestial.32) from the Viceroy.

title: A stern letter
summary: The Viceroy complains that the ruler's merchants cheat Cathay's traders. Curbing the guilds in the capital and in the cities of two or three vassals pleases Cathay most (150 grace), but costs city taxes for ten years and may anger the vassals (celestial.33). Setting the spymaster on the worst cheats pleases Cathay less (50) and taxes only the capital, and keeps the spymaster busy for a while unless cunning. Ignoring it costs 150 grace.

title: The guilds of my cities
summary: The vassal hears that the liege curbed the merchants of one of the vassal's cities to please Cathay. A public protest wins a reputation for standing up for the vassals' rights, angers the liege and tells the liege (celestial.34); silence costs a little prestige.

title: A vassal protests
summary: The vassal's protest costs the liege prestige and sours the vassal.

title: A guest from the Celestial Court
summary: Hidden. A courtier who came from Cathay to this court, and is neither an escaped noble nor a refugee, gives a verdict on the stay, once: praise (celestial.41) from a guest who does not dislike the host, likelier when host and guest share virtues, vices, looks, wit, learning or pastimes; scorn (celestial.42); or nothing.

title: Talk until dawn
summary: The guest writes home in praise of the host: 150 grace, or 100 grace, prestige and perhaps pride for spreading the word.

title: A slip of the tongue
summary: The guest storms off, swearing the Emperor will hear of an insult: 100 grace lost, or the guest is put under house arrest and the host becomes arbitrary or cruel.

title: Wanderlust
summary: Hidden. A playable lord at peace with Cathay, with at least two courtiers who could travel (not eastern, unlanded, not the heir, not a commander), hears one of them, preferably one Cathay likes, ask to go east (celestial.51). Likelier while Cathay thrives, rarer while it suffers or keeps to itself.

title: The courtier asks
summary: Hidden. Puts the request to the lord (celestial.52) with the courtier as FROM.

title: A journey east
summary: The courtier begs to go to the Jade Viceroy's court for the lord's glory. The lord may send the courtier, or someone else: a spouse, lover or friend if one can go, else any courtier; a child who is not the heir, else any courtier. Each shows whether Cathay likes the traveller. The traveller leaves for the Viceroy's court for about a year and comes home (celestial.53). Or the lord says no.

calls: celestial.54; celestial.55; celestial.56; celestial.57; celestial.58; celestial.59; celestial.61
title: Home from the East
summary: Hidden. The traveller comes home to the lord, or, if the lord has died, to whoever holds the lord's old capital, and that lord hears how it went: - great (celestial.54) or good (celestial.55), likelier for a pleasant, diplomatic, well-liked traveller while Cathay thrives; - so-so (celestial.56); - bad (celestial.57) or terrible (celestial.58), likelier for a dull, clumsy or disliked traveller while Cathay suffers; - a Cathayan lover (celestial.59), for an unattached traveller of a people with women; - a longing to go back for good (celestial.61), for an unlanded traveller who is not the lord's spouse.

title: Gifts from the East
summary: The traveller comes home in triumph: medium grace and 25 gold for the lord, pride and perhaps bravery for the traveller. Half the time, once per life and only if the lord holds no Cathayan treasure, the Viceroy sent one along.

title: Tales from the East
summary: The traveller brings coins and stories: minor grace, and perhaps patience.

title: A letter of greeting
summary: A tired traveller, a sealed letter from the Viceroy: trivial grace.

title: A tirade
summary: The traveller hated it: trivial grace lost, and perhaps a stressed traveller.

title: A disgrace
summary: The traveller shamed the lord at the Viceroy's court: minor grace lost, a shy traveller, and perhaps a depressed one.

title: Someone from Taharq
summary: Hidden. Creates the traveller's Cathayan lover, of the Viceroy's culture and faith (a woman for a man, a man for a woman), makes them lovers and gives the traveller the wish to marry; the lord meets the lover (celestial.60).

title: A guest from the East
summary: The traveller brings home a Cathayan lover. The lord may welcome the lover to court, or send the lover away, which the traveller will not forgive (a stressed traveller turns depressed). Either way, medium grace.

title: The call of the East
summary: The traveller wants to go back to Cathay for good. Letting them go (with spouse and young children of their own) earns major grace; refusing angers them, a diplomat can soften it, and a lord they love deeply can plead with them to stay. Each refusal earns medium grace for the courtesy shown at the Viceroy's court.

title: Word from Taharq
summary: The traveller died abroad (not by leaving for Cathay or vanishing), and the Viceroy sends condolences.

title: Clean-up
summary: Hidden. Clears the journey flag, whatever became of the traveller, so the lord may send someone again.

title: The Emperor seeks a trading partner
summary: Hidden. One year in twenty, unless Cathay keeps to itself or suffers famine or plague, the Jade Viceroy calls the playable lords of one rank (counts, dukes, kings or emperors, each rank at most once in fifteen years) with land on the roads east to a contest, if at least two qualify; up to five take part (celestial.71). Dukes and above may be set to found a city on the roads (if a holding there is free), with five years to do it (celestial.76); anyone may be set to win the most renown in five years, with a word on who leads after half the time (celestial.78) and the verdict at the end (celestial.80).

title: The Emperor's decree
summary: The Viceroy announces the contest and its terms to each contestant.

title: Breaking ground
summary: Hidden. A contestant set to found a city starts building one in a province on the roads east.

title: A city on the road east
summary: Hidden. The first contestant to finish such a city wins; the Viceroy hears of it (celestial.74).

title: The Viceroy names the winner
summary: Hidden. Sends the verdict (celestial.75) to every contestant, and marks the contest as won.

title: The new city
summary: The founder of the city wins the contest (celestial_contest_prize_effect); the others lose 100 grace.

title: Five years pass
summary: Hidden. If no contestant founded a city, they all hear of the Emperor's displeasure (celestial.77).

title: No city rises
summary: Nobody founded a city: every contestant loses 250 grace.

title: Halfway
summary: Hidden. Measures how much renown each contestant has won so far, and tells each who leads (celestial.79).

title: Rumours from the East
summary: The contestant hears who the Viceroy thinks most worthy so far.

title: The verdict
summary: Hidden. The contestant who won the most renown in five years wins (a tie is settled by lot), and every contestant hears the verdict (celestial.81).

title: The most worthy
summary: The winner gains the prize (celestial_contest_prize_effect); the others lose 100 grace.

title: Safety clean-up
summary: Hidden. Clears a contestant's flags if the contest never ended (the Viceroy died or changed before the verdict).

title: A fugitive arrives
summary: Hidden. Once in a lord's life, a Cathayan noble whose family was put to death by the Dragon Emperor's order comes to the court seeking asylum (celestial.86). Rare for AI lords.

title: The fugitive asks
summary: Hidden. Puts the plea to the lord (celestial.87) with the fugitive as FROM.

title: A plea for asylum
summary: The fugitive begs for refuge. Sheltering them earns gratitude, and either the Viceroy finds out (celestial.88) or, in time, the fugitive moves on with thanks (celestial.90). Sheltering them while secretly writing to the Viceroy hands them over (celestial.91), unless someone warns them (celestial.92). Or the lord sends them away.

title: The Viceroy hears of it
summary: Hidden. Sends the Viceroy's demand (celestial.89).

title: The Viceroy's demand
summary: The Viceroy demands the fugitive. Giving them up hands them over (celestial.91); refusing costs major grace, and the Emperor's assassins may strike (celestial.93) or the fugitive moves on in time (celestial.90).

title: A grateful farewell
summary: No one came for the fugitive, who moves on. Once per life, if the lord holds no Cathayan treasure, the fugitive leaves an heirloom (a dragon amulet, a silk shroud or a small figurine); otherwise a purse of gold.

title: Handed over
summary: The Viceroy's guards take the fugitive east to be executed: medium grace.

title: Warned
summary: Someone warned the fugitive, who fled the night before the guards came: minor grace lost.

title: A length of silk
summary: The Emperor's assassins strangle the fugitive with a silk cord.

title: A refugee flees west
summary: Hidden. While Cathay suffers war, invasion, famine or plague, a trained Cathayan flees west to a lord's court: an administrator or master engineer (if the court lacks one), a strategist, or a physician (Reapers, if the court lacks one). Likelier for lords on the roads east; rarer under an isolationist Cathay and in a civil war, famine or plague. Once per twenty years (celestial.98).

title: The refugee arrives
summary: Hidden. Brings the refugee before the lord (celestial.97) with the refugee as FROM.

title: A refugee from the East
summary: A Cathayan who fled the troubles at home begs to serve the lord: as administrator or master engineer (the post brings its own bonus, better if Cathay was in a golden age when they were trained), as commander, or as court physician. A lord who turns them away leaves them to die on the road.

title: Room for another refugee
summary: Hidden. Twenty years on, another refugee may come (celestial.95).

title: A scholar on the road
summary: Once in a lord's life, a scholar of the Celestial Court reaches a town of the lord's on the roads east and offers to teach one of the lord's children (the heir if possible). A cannibal lord may have the scholar for dinner instead.

title: The scholar's lessons
summary: The scholar offers, for a fee, to teach the child to read quickly (learning), the classics of the Celestial Court (erudite), surgery and poetry (poet), or to wake a dull child's curiosity. A child taught the classics may come to secretly worship the Celestial Dragon. Sending the scholar away costs a little prestige.

title: A caravan factor calls
summary: Once in a lord's life, a factor of the Cathayan caravan houses asks the lord to fund a trade office in a city of the realm on the roads east (trade value and city taxes for 50 years). A generous lord may give the factor the city itself (more trade for 100 years, and the Jade Viceroy's thanks), outraging its burgher. A cannibal lord may have the factor for dinner and keep the purse.

title: The caravan houses want their gold
summary: A lord who borrowed from the caravan houses (borrow_from_caravan_houses in WHG_cathay_decisions.txt) is reminded of the debt. Paying now clears it; putting it off means the caravans pass the lord's markets by for a while.

title: The journey east
summary: The traveller takes leave and sets out for Grand Cathay.

title: Planning the road
summary: Hidden. The farther the traveller's capital lies from the Gnoblar country at Cathay's western edge, the more scenes the road east holds (one to four), and the more great dangers: the Warpstone Desert always, the Mountains of Mourn from 500, the Dark Lands from 900. Then the preparations (kowtow.4).

title: Preparing the road
summary: Old caravan masters warn the traveller: the Warpstone Desert kills without wards, the Ogres of the Mountains of Mourn take their tithe or the caravan, and the Dark Lands burn. Buy wards (75 gold), pay the tithe ahead (75), both (150), take ship under the Sea Dragon's flag (200, a port is needed: a typhoon, and corsairs from far away, instead of the overland dangers), or trust to the gods.

title: On the road
summary: Hidden. With a great danger still ahead, half the time (always once the scenes run out) the traveller meets it (kowtow_send_leg_effect). Otherwise rolls the next road scene, each at most once per journey: rain and grief, a lord's invitation (far from Cathay only), a band on the road (those three only overland), homesickness or a pedlar. With no scenes or dangers left, or none that fits, the traveller reaches Cathay (kowtow.50).

title: Rain on the road
summary: Rain keeps the caravan in camp, and the traveller remembers a dead parent or sibling: honour them (honouring the dead) or press on (carrying on).

title: An invitation
summary: A count or duke on the roads east invites the traveller to stay. A schemer may use a rival's welcome to poison them (kowtow.23); otherwise accept (kowtow.21) or keep to the tent.

title: The host's table
summary: A pleasant stay; or a new friendship with the host; or a rival's poisoned cup, which kills half the time and otherwise leaves the traveller in a ditch (kowtow.22).

title: A warning in the ditch
summary: The traveller survives the rival's poison with a warning and a sick stomach (food poisoning with The Reaper's Due, else poisoned).

title: Fatal hospitality
summary: The schemer's poison plot at a rival's table: the rival dies and the schemer slips away (likelier with high intrigue); both die; or the plot is found out and the schemer is cut down.

title: A band on the road
summary: Hidden. Picks who the traveller meets by Cathay's state and makes their captain (kowtow_road_captain_effect): hobgoblin raiders taking a toll while Cathay is at war or in unrest (kowtow.31), ogre sell-swords offering an escort in peace or unrest (kowtow.32), or starving Cathayan deserters in famine or plague (kowtow.33).

title: A toll at the bridge
summary: Hobgoblin raiders demand a toll: pay, fight your way through (escape, a maiming, or death, by strength and skill), or, for an impaler, spear the chief.

title: Ogres for hire
summary: Ogre sell-swords mistake the traveller's caravan for the one that hired them: hire them as bodyguards (hired body guards, three years) or send them on.

title: Starving deserters
summary: Starving Cathayan soldiers bar the road: share the food (a friend, the kind, charity), take their captain into service, or pass them by.

title: Homesick
summary: The traveller misses someone at home (a lover, spouse, parent, child or friend) and may pay a courier to carry a letter (kowtow.41).

title: A letter from the road
summary: The one missed reads the traveller's letter (opinion: love letters, pen pal or delighted parent). Also used by the witch hunter on the road.

title: A pedlar on the road
summary: A smooth-talking Cathayan pedlar offers a Cathayan treasure: buy it, take the pedlar into service (kind), have the guards take it (deceitful), or wave the pedlar off.

title: The Warpstone Desert
summary: The last great danger overland. With wards the caravan crosses the green dust unharmed. Without, push on (warp sickness, a madness, or death), hire an oasis guide (100 gold) or take the long way round (half a year).

title: The Mountains of Mourn
summary: The Ogres of the Mountains of Mourn take a tithe from every caravan. If it was paid ahead, an Ogre escort takes the caravan through the passes. If not, the Ogres block the pass: pay double (150 gold), feast them and bargain (50 gold and diplomacy), fight through (martial: renown, wounds, or the cooking pot) or turn for home.

title: The Dark Lands
summary: Lava, ash and earthquakes, Chaos Dwarf slavers and hobgoblin wolf riders. Go by night on the old roads (intrigue), hire hobgoblin guides (60 gold, and the word of a hobgoblin), or march hard with the escort (martial).

title: The typhoon
summary: At sea a typhoon falls on the fleet. Trust the junk's captain, or pray.

title: Corsairs
summary: From far away the ship passes the coasts of the Southlands, where Druchii black arks and pirates hunt. Trust the Sea Dragon's war junks, pay them off (100 gold), or fight on deck (martial).

title: Into Grand Cathay
summary: The caravan reaches Grand Cathay at Shang-Yang, the Iron Dragon's city, or the ship docks at Fu-Chow, the Sea Dragon's port, and the traveller goes on to Wei-Jin. One who braved the great dangers overland is honoured for it: renown, and the Jade Dragon's regard. Two scenes in Cathay follow (kowtow.51).

title: In Wei-Jin
summary: Hidden. Rolls the next scene in Cathay, each at most once: the game of stones, a temple of the Celestial Dragons, the Annals of the Jade Sages or the markets. With no scenes left, or none that fits, the audience comes (kowtow.60).

title: The game of stones
summary: Courtiers play the game of black and white stones in a garden: a gamer shows how it is done (gold, proud), anyone else tries their luck, or enjoys the garden (patient or humble). Playing pleases the Emperor.

title: A temple of the Celestial Dragons
summary: The traveller comes upon a rite to the Celestial Dragons: study it from afar (sympathy for the eastern faiths), join in (a zealot of another faith loses the zeal; pleases the Emperor), denounce it (piety; displeases the Emperor), or study the temple's script (learning).

title: The Annals of the Jade Sages
summary: Ministers offer to read the Annals of the Jade Sages with the traveller: listen (pleases the Emperor), show off knowing them already (poet or scholar; prestige), or ask for a tour of the palace (may gain stewardship; displeases the Emperor).

title: The markets of Wei-Jin
summary: The traveller walks the markets: taste the food (may turn gluttonous; pleases the Emperor), buy a Cathayan treasure (pleases the Emperor), have it stolen (intrigue 15 or elusive shadow; displeases the Emperor), or go back to the lodgings.

title: Before the Celestial Throne
summary: The audience, held by Yuan Bo the Jade Dragon while the Emperor is away. The impression adds half the traveller's diplomacy, the rank (king +7, emperor +14) and Cathay's regard (+5 liked, -5 disliked) to the scenes in Cathay and the road, and sets the odds: the traveller bows before a painting of the absent Emperor (kowtow 1), before his empty throne with the Jade Dragon beside it (kowtow 2) or receives the Jade Dragon's own blessing (kowtow 3). Each kowtow gives 100 grace and costs prestige by rank (kowtow_prestige_cost_effect). After a painting, the traveller may storm out instead (the Asur still lose half the price in pride).

title: Cathay closes its gates
summary: Hidden. When Cathay turns isolationist, every lord on the way to kowtow turns back (kowtow_abort_effect, kowtow.71).

title: The journey cut short
summary: The traveller learns the journey to Cathay is over: war, or Cathay has closed its gates. The lord may set out again later.

title: War calls the traveller home
summary: Hidden. A lord on the way to kowtow who goes to war, or is attacked, turns back (kowtow_abort_effect, kowtow.71).

title: An expedition east
summary: A realm that does not serve Chaos picks what it marches on Cathay for: gold, slaves, a place at the court or Cathay's learning. The goal flag decides what invasion_of_cathay_cb pays out on success.

title: News from Cathay: an expedition marches east
summary: The text follows the invader's goal.

title: News from Cathay: an expedition comes home victorious
summary: The text follows the invader's goal.

title: News from Cathay: Chaos marches on the Dragon Throne
summary: would sit on the throne is event_target:invasion_of_cathay_claimant.

title: The raiders' year
summary: Hidden. Once a year, a raiding lord's war bands come home. A lord who may no longer raid (a vassal now, landless, or forbidden to loot) calls them back (cathayraid.2); otherwise one outcome is picked and shown (cathayraid.3).

title: The raids are over
summary: The lord can no longer send raiders east. Raids may start again in five years.

title: The raiders return
summary: One of eight outcomes, set by cathayraid_pick_outcome_effect: plain loot, rich loot, a ransomed mandarin, a disaster, a captive, a siege engineer, a treasure of Cathay (once per lifetime) or a pair of pandas.

title: A warning from the Viceroy
summary: Letter sent when a lord starts raiding Cathay: the Jade Viceroy warns that the Dragon Throne will not suffer it for long.

title: The pandas die
summary: Twenty-odd years after they were brought west, the pandas die without young. A lord may mourn them hard.

title: A new house on the Dragon Throne
summary: Hidden. Names the empire after the new house, unless the war that set it up already chose a name (rename_override). Ends the peace pacts, grace timers and trade contracts of the old house, frees its tributaries (was_tributary_of_cathay, read by the news in jd_chinese_status_and_policy_events) and wipes the kowtow honours.

title: Cathay's name and government at game start
summary: Hidden. Makes sure Cathay and its western governor run the Celestial bureaucracy, and that Cathay under the Dragon Emperor is called Cathay. Runs once per game.

title: A new Emperor picks a policy
summary: Hidden. The new ruler of Cathay chooses to keep the empire open, close it or turn expansionist, swayed by its state, by trends the last reign or war left (cathay_isolationist_trend, cathay_expansionist_trend) and by past defeats. Lords within reach hear of the new reign (cathaystate.11).

title: News from Cathay: a new Emperor
summary: The old Emperor is gone; the news tells whether a new house rules and whether the policy changed. Tributaries of the old house learn they are free, and a peace deal with the old house is void.

title: Cathay changes its policy
summary: Hidden. Lords within reach hear of it (cathaystate.16), unless the change came with a new Emperor (cathaystate.11 tells of both).

title: News from Cathay: a new policy
summary: Cathay has put aside its ways. The gates of the Great Bastion stand open again, and the jade, silk and black powder of the east flow west to any lord with gold...

title: The Dragon Emperor changes his mind
summary: Hidden. The Dragon Emperor never dies, so the policy that cathaystate.10 picks for a new Emperor would last forever. Instead, at most once every 15 years, he may open or close the borders, or march west to defend Cathay's colonies, hunt the exiles who fled him or punish those who sacked Cathay (wh_cathay_events.txt does the marching). The news comes from cathaystate.15.

title: Cathay's state changes
summary: Hidden. Clears the invasion timers and tells lords within reach (cathaystate.21), unless the change has news of its own.

title: News from Cathay: the empire's state
summary: . Order returns to the provinces of Grand Cathay, and the caravans set out west once more.

title: The roads east follow Cathay's fortune
summary: Hidden. Sets the worth of the roads east from Cathay's status and policy (cathaystate_road_values_effect).

title: The roads east at game start
summary: Hidden. Sets the worth of the roads east once, for the host of a new game.

title: Peace returns to Cathay
summary: Hidden. Unrest, famine, plague or a golden age ends and Cathay is stable again, the more likely the longer the status has lasted. News through cathaystate.20.

title: Unrest in Cathay
summary: Hidden. Peasant risings and rebel sects; likelier after long hardship and under a foreign Emperor, rare in a golden age.

title: Famine in Cathay
summary: Hidden. No more than one famine in ninety years, never early in a golden age.

title: Plague in Cathay
summary: Hidden. No more than one plague in ninety years, never early in a golden age.

title: A golden age dawns
summary: Hidden. Only from stability, about once in two to two and a half centuries.

title: The Hobgoblin hordes invade
summary: Hidden. The khans of the eastern steppe unite and break through the Great Bastion. Likelier when Cathay is weak, rarer after each of their victories and never under a hobgoblin Emperor. Lords within reach hear of it (cathaystate.41).

title: News from Cathay: the Hobgoblin hordes
summary: With Cathay already suffering from the , a great Hobgoblin horde has seized its chance and crossed the Great Bastion into the north. Will the wolf riders of...

title: The Hobgoblin war ends
summary: Hidden. The longer the war, the likelier its end. Cathay wins (likelier after a golden age) or the hordes win (likelier after hardship, or when a hobgoblin khan of the map leads them). A victorious horde is paid off by the Dragon Emperor; once the Dragon Throne has fallen, the khan or his kin takes it. Exiles may flee west afterwards.

title: News from Cathay: the hordes are beaten
summary: After years of war and battles of hundreds of thousands, the armies of Cathay have won a decisive victory near . The Hobgoblin Khagan is slain, his wolf riders...

title: News from Cathay: the hordes triumph
summary: The Dragon Emperor paid them off, or a hobgoblin now sits on the Dragon Throne; a peace deal with the old house is void.

title: The Man-chu horsemen invade
summary: Hidden. The Man-chu, Hung horse-tribes of the north-east, unite under a khagan and ride into Cathay. Likelier when Cathay is weak, never under a Man-chu Emperor. Lords within reach hear of it (cathaystate.51).

title: News from Cathay: the Man-chu horsemen
summary: With Cathay already suffering from the , a new misfortune has struck: the Man-chu have united under a Chaos-sworn Khagan and their horsemen pour into the...

title: The Man-chu war ends
summary: Hidden. As cathaystate.42: Cathay wins, or the horsemen win and are driven back by the Dragon Emperor at a terrible price; once the Dragon Throne has fallen, their khagan takes it.

title: News from Cathay: the horsemen are beaten
summary: After years of war and battles of hundreds of thousands, the armies of Cathay have won a decisive victory near . The Man-chu Khagan is slain, his chosen riders...

title: News from Cathay: the horsemen triumph
summary: After years of war and battles of hundreds of thousands, the Man-chu stand triumphant. The last battle was fought near , and now their Khagan sits upon the...

title: Civil war in Cathay
summary: Hidden. Long unrest turns into open war between the loyalists and rebel governors, generals and sects; rare when Cathay is stable. Lords within reach hear of it (cathaystate.61).

title: News from Cathay: civil war
summary: The long Unrest in Cathay has flared into open Civil War! Many say that  is weak and has lost the Mandate of Heaven. While shelters in , rebel armies storm...

title: The civil war ends
summary: Hidden. After at least two years, likelier the longer it lasts. The loyalists win (always under the Dragon Emperor), or, once the Dragon Throne has fallen, a rebel general founds a new house (likelier against a foreign Emperor) or a pretender of the old house takes the throne. Rebel generals and exiles may head west afterwards.

title: News from Cathay: the loyalists win
summary: The Cathayan Civil War has ended.  has crushed the main rebel army in , ending long years of war between loyalists, rabble-rousing monks, pretenders and an...

title: News from Cathay: a new house
summary: A rebel general has founded a new house; a foreign house may have been thrown out. A peace deal with the old house is void.

title: News from Cathay: a pretender of the old house
summary: After long years of war and shifting alliances, the Cathayan Civil War is over. The old court has fallen, and , a pretender of the , now sits upon the Dragon...

title: The Emperor's kin go home
summary: Hidden. At the start of a new game, unlanded kin of the Emperor and of his predecessor who are on the map return to Cathay.

title: A cultist casts off the mask
summary: Sent by the rising cult leader (chaoscult.2) to every cultist and secret Chaos worshipper in the defending realm. They convert to their secret faith and leave the cult; landed ones join the revolt against their independent liege (or liege's liege) with an independence war.

title: The cult rises
summary: The cult leader proclaims their faith. They become a devout leader, break away from a top liege outside the cult with an independence war, and call on every cultist in that realm to rise too (chaoscult.1).

title: The truth revealed
summary: A revealed cult leader flips the provinces where their cult has a secret community to the open faith.

title: A vassal turns heretic
summary: Tells a liege that a vassal was a secret servant of Chaos all along. Skipped for those already taking part in the uprising.

title: Prepare the grounds: mission ping
summary: Hidden. The grand master hands the mission to the cultist (chaoscult.11).

title: Prepare the grounds: the mission
summary: The cult asks for a secret cell in a chosen province before it can rise.

title: Prepare the grounds: clear the lock
summary: Hidden. Lets the cultist try the same province again.

title: A cell is founded
summary: The cultist starts a cell in the target province. Diplomacy helps; a province outside the cultist's own demesne takes longer and goes worse. The outcome arrives after 300 (own) or 500 days: easy (chaoscult.16), going well (17) or struggling (18). chaoscult.14 watches the province meanwhile.

title: Watch the province
summary: Hidden, monthly. If the target province leaves the realm, the cell is lost (chaoscult.15).

title: The province is lost
summary: The cell cannot be kept up from abroad. The mission fails.

title: The faithful flock in
summary: The cell grows with ease and is founded in about 150 days (chaoscult.19).

title: The cell grows
summary: Good progress; the cell is founded later (chaoscult.19).

title: The cell struggles
summary: Pay to keep it going (founded after about 450 days, chaoscult.19) or give up and fail the mission.

title: The cell is founded
summary: The province gets a secret community of the cultist's god. Completes the mission.

title: Dinner with an open mind
summary: First step of recruiting someone into a Chaos cult (decisions in wh_cult_societies_decisions.txt and the recruitment events in WHG_society_events.txt, society.13). The recruiter sounds out the target's faith. Agreeing moves on (chaoscult.21); refusing tells the recruiter (chaoscult.22). Each god's recruits favour different traits.

title: Safety ping: recruiter still there?
summary: Hidden. Passes the recruit's answer on if the recruiter is alive and still a cultist, otherwise the recruit loses contact (chaoscult.32).

title: The recruiter weighs the answer
summary: Go on to the strange idol (chaoscult.23), or give up.

title: A strange idol
summary: The recruiter shares more radical ideas and a gift. Keeping it shows willingness; refusing ends it. Either answer goes back through chaoscult.24.

title: Safety ping: the offer
summary: Hidden. Same check as chaoscult.21 before chaoscult.25.

title: Make the offer?
summary: A willing recruit can be asked to join (chaoscult.26). An unwilling one ends the attempt.

title: The question
summary: The recruiter reveals the truth. Saying yes (chaoscult.27) promises help with the recruit's own trouble; no (chaoscult.28) ends it.

title: Safety ping: yes
summary: Hidden. Tells the recruiter (chaoscult.30), or chaoscult.32.

title: Safety ping: no
summary: Hidden. Tells the recruiter (chaoscult.29), or chaoscult.32.

title: The recruit refused
summary: Notification.

title: The recruit said yes
summary: The recruiter picks a senior cultist as the inductor and confirms (chaoscult.31).

title: The promise
summary: The recruit hears what the god offers; forbidden study follows (chaoscult.33).

title: Contact lost
summary: The recruiter has died or turned away. Notification.

title: Forbidden books
summary: The recruit studies the occult and loses zealotry. The mark follows (chaoscult.34).

title: The mark in blood
summary: A mark of the god appears on the recruit's door. Carving it into the arm brings the inductor (chaoscult.35); refusing ends it (chaoscult.48 and a failure letter to the recruiter).

title: Find the inductor
summary: Hidden. Finds a free senior cultist if none is set and starts the letter step through chaoscult.36.

summary: Hidden. Sends the recruiter the outcome letter (chaoscult.50).

title: Recruitment without an inductor
summary: Hidden. The inductor died before the end (fired from mnm_assassins_events.txt and the cult decisions). Finds the grand master of the cult (or the Assassins or Clan Eshin) to write instead (chaoscult.56).

title: The grand master writes
summary: Hidden. Sends the recruit the letter (chaoscult.57).

title: A letter from the grand master
summary: Join as a member or sleeper agent, or refuse and anger the grand master.

title: The soul darkens
summary: Hidden. Every two years a Chaos cultist who has been in the cult for three years takes a small or big step towards Chaos. A known cultist is hunted one time in eleven, a highly suspect one one time in 34 (chaoscult.440).

summary: The spouse dies by lightning.

summary: Hidden. From the society power on the victim: a mild, dangerous or lethal disease (stronger for the grand master and the learned). The curser hears back once it shows (chaoscult.132).

title: The curse takes hold
summary: Notification for the curser.

summary: Hidden. From the society power. Creates a witch or warlock, young or old, who joins the cult and comes to court (chaoscult.136).

summary: Hidden. Leads to the introduction (chaoscult.137).

summary: Introduction at court.

title: The hunters close in (hidden)
summary: Salvaged from vanilla MNM.7854 (mnm_devil_worshipers_events.txt), which ran on the society pulse list and from the unused soul corruption effect. A Chaos cultist who is known for what he is, or highly suspect, or whom another cultist has betrayed, is tracked down. Picks the hunters: a Sister of Sigmar, a mob with torches (only for one with a familiar), two Templars of the Silver Hammer, a lone witch hunter or the knights of a templar order; the same ones come back the second time. A bedridden cultist is simply taken. Also picks a fellow cultist to blame. Then chaoscult.441.

title: The hunters come
summary: Fight (combat skill, strength and wits help), bribe (diplomacy and looks help; the faithful may drag the cultist to the stake instead), call on the cult's god with a child's life (a major favour and a child at court), or give them another cultist's name (half the time they burn the cultist anyway, and the other cultist is hunted next). A bedridden cultist burns.

title: The strain of the mask
summary: Hidden, on_society_bi_yearly_pulse. A stressed or depressed cultist is asked to a private rite by a fellow cultist who likes him (a friend, or someone he is drawn to): at court first, then in the realm, then anywhere in reach.

title: The strain of the mask: bounce
summary: Hidden. Sends the invitation back to the cultist (chaoscult.452).

title: A rite for two
summary: The fellow cultist's rite lifts the cultist's stress and despair, and the fellow's too. He can take the fellow as a friend, confess that he wants more (the courtship of assassins.406), or keep the friendship as it is.

title: Cracks in the mask
summary: Hidden, on_society_bi_yearly_pulse. A cultist whom people have begun to notice has a flaw that may give him away: too honest, too wrathful, too careless, too trusting or too clumsy at intrigue. A fellow cultist without that flaw notices (chaoscult.456).

title: A danger to us all
summary: The fellow cultist sees the flaw. He offers to help for nothing, for the cult's favour, or keeps out of it. Turning away clears the flaw flags.

title: A word in private
summary: The flawed cultist hears the offer and accepts it (paying the cult's favour if asked), or waves it away (chaoscult.460). Lessons go well half the time, more with the teacher's intrigue (chaoscult.458), or not (chaoscult.459).

title: A diligent student
summary: The lessons worked. The teacher gains favour if he was paid, and the student loses the flaw (chaoscult.461).

title: Some can't be taught
summary: The lessons failed. The teacher still keeps the favour he was paid (chaoscult.462 for the student).

title: The fool waves me off
summary: The flawed cultist refused the help.

title: The mask holds
summary: The student loses the flaw (or gains intrigue) and draws less suspicion.

title: What I am
summary: The student could not change.

title: A child of the cult
summary: Hidden, on_adolescence. A child whose educator, guardian or parent (who must be his liege) is a Chaos cultist may be drawn into the cult's faith. The educator comes first, then the guardian, then the mother, then the father.

title: The child is ready
summary: The cultist decides whether to teach the child the cult's secret rhymes (chaoscult.467) or leave the child be. Cowards and the paranoid hold back.

title: The old rhymes
summary: The child hears the cult's secret rhymes and the truth behind them. He may take to them (secret faith, chaoscult.468), keep the secret for love of the teacher (chaoscult.469), or scorn it (chaoscult.470).

title: One of us
summary: The child took to the cult's faith.

title: Our little secret
summary: The child keeps the secret but is not won over yet.

title: The child recoils
summary: The child scorned the rhymes. The cultist can try once more, patiently (chaoscult.471): a patient cultist may always try, anyone else only when not out of patience, and then runs out of it. Or let it be.

title: Questions, not lectures
summary: The cultist asks the child questions this time. The child comes round (chaoscult.468) or turns zealous for the true gods, takes the cultist as a rival and may tell a priest (chaoscult.472).

title: The child turns away
summary: The child is now zealous for the true gods and a rival. One time in three the child tells a priest, and suspicion grows.

title: Cold feet
summary: On_society_bi_yearly_pulse, mostly for players (AI weight x0.05). A fellow cultist in reach, most likely a paranoid or stressed one, wants to leave the cult. The cultist argues for the brotherhood or the god's eye, soothes him (gregarious only), lets him go, or makes sure he never talks (chaoscult.476 judges the arguments).

title: Cold feet: the answer
summary: The worried cultist stays (a soothed one also loses paranoia and stress) or still means to leave: let him go, or silence him after all.

title: The painter from Tilea
summary: On_yearly_pulse, once per life. A Chaos cultist who owns neither painting hears of a Tilean master and may commission a landscape (chaoscult.481), if a fellow cultist lives in his realm to see it.

title: The unveiling
summary: The painting is done. Ask the painter to hide the god's signs in it (usually fine, but he may take fright and talk), paint them in yourself (60% fine, chaoscult.482; else a daub, chaoscult.483), or hang it as is.

title: One who sees
summary: A fellow cultist of higher rank (or any in the realm) reads the hidden signs and slips the cultist the god's token: the painting, the cult's favour and a budding friendship.

title: A daub
summary: The cultist's own brushwork ruined the painting. Keep it (a strange piece that only the bold admire) or hide it away and lose face.

title: The painter talks
summary: The painter recognised the signs and took fright. The painting is delivered without them, but the painter is talking in the taverns.

title: 491 The soul darkens
summary: Hidden. Some days after a corrupting deed the god's mark settles on the soul: a major (490) or minor (491) roll of trait changes per god (chaos_corruption_major/minor_roll_effect), then a notice to a player (chaoscult.492). Rarely (4% major, 1% minor, doubled for the mad) the deed leaves a door open and something starts to whisper (chaoscult.493).

title: The soul darkens: notice
summary: Something has changed in you since the blood was spilt. Your temper runs hotter and your pity thinner, and at night you dream of a brass throne on a mountain...

title: Whispers in the dark
summary: A voice speaks in dreams and quiet hours. Listen (chaoscult.494), hold to the faith (half the time it fades), raise a warding relic (it falls silent), or, for the god's own, open the door at once (chaoscult.495).

title: The bargain
summary: The voice asks to be let in. Refusing may not be enough (half the time it takes its seat anyway).

title: Something behind the eyes
summary: Possessed, and given a sliver of the daemon's gift by the god it serves.

title: A cultist no longer
summary: Hidden. One who converts to a Chaos, necromantic or Shadowmen faith loses the known satanist and known witch modifiers: nothing to hide any more.

title: Nurgle's physician
summary: A Nurgle cultist who is court physician gives the healthy liege a gift of Nurgle (cultpath.6). At most once every two and a half years.

title: The gift takes hold
summary: Hidden. The liege falls ill.

title: The grand master's word
summary: Hidden. Sends the mission to the member (cultpath.31).

title: The focus the god loves
summary: The member is told to take up one of the two focuses the god loves: Nurgle family or business, Slaanesh seduction or carousing, Tzeentch scholarship or intrigue, Khorne war or hunting, Undivided war or rulership. Taking it up ends the mission (cultpath.32).

title: The god is pleased
summary: The member takes up the focus the mission asked for, and the mission ends.

summary: Hidden. Sends the first-blood duel mission to the member (cultpath.41).

title: First blood
summary: Draw a brother's blood in a duel; the healthiest, closest warrior is picked first.

title: The grand master's word
summary: Hidden. Sends the duel-to-the-death mission to the member (cultpath.43).

title: A skull for the Skull Throne
summary: Slay a foe in a duel: a rival first, else a vassal or courtier of the member's own realm who is not of the cult. Was broken: it looked only for cult members who were not in the cult, so nearly always fell back to a rival or found no one.

title: The grand master's word
summary: Hidden. Sends the seduction mission to the member (cultpath.51).

title: A seduction for the Dark Prince
summary: Seduce a ruler of the member's faith within reach, one who would be drawn to the member. Was broken for women: it picked another woman.

title: Into the furnace
summary: A prisoner is thrown into Hashut's furnace. A Dawi of the Ancestor Gods is the prize offering, then a captive lord, then anyone else. Outside a grand rite each offering adds a point of Hashut's favour; in a grand rite Hashut answers.

title: The offering burns
summary: The offering dies in the molten metal. Its dynasty hates the sacrificer, and killing close kin makes the sacrificer a kinslayer. The truly undying cheat the furnace.

title: A prisoner is dragged to the furnace
summary: Hidden step that turns a chosen prisoner into the FROM of dawizharr.1.

title: The grand sacrifice
summary: The acolytes ready the ziggurat's furnaces. The ruler offers the slaves of a factory or of the levy pens (each costs a level of that building), or a prisoner. The rite costs 200 gold and Hashut will not hear another for about four years.

title: The slaves go into the fire
summary: Bull Centaurs herd a mass of slaves into the furnace. Feeds Hashut and draws his answer.

title: The furnaces are cold
summary: Four years without an offering. The ruler can give up a level of a slave building, drag a prisoner to the furnace, or let vassals and priests turn against them (must_sacrifice_hashut, lifted by the next sacrifice).

title: Hashut offers gifts
summary: The brazen idol speaks and offers a choice: K'daai to burn the ruler's foes, a body like a Bull Centaur's, Hashut's fire on the land, or (for a sorcerer) deeper mastery of the Winds.

title: A K'daai rises from the furnace
summary: A daemon of fire and iron climbs out of the molten pit and swears itself to the ruler.

title: Hashut sends a Great Taurus
summary: A Great Taurus, one of Hashut's favoured beasts, lands outside the temple. Never rolled for someone who already rides one.

title: Visions of glory
summary: The molten metal shows the ruler wealth and power. One time in four, if the ruler has none, a rune of Hashut's blood cools out of the metal (dawizharr_bloodhashut).

title: His greatest child
summary: Hashut's voice praises the ruler, who grows proud.

title: A crown of fire
summary: Hashut sends visions that burn the ruler's mind (lunacy, mutate.5).

title: A gush of molten metal
summary: The furnace spits in the ruler's face. Never rolled for the already disfigured.

title: Silence
summary: Hashut ignores the offering.

title: Bull Centaurs at the foot of the ziggurat
summary: A regiment of Bull Centaurs waits outside the temple to serve the ruler. (Restored from the old grand sacrifice results.)

title: Hashut's wrath
summary: A cloud of red smoke forces itself down the ruler's throat (hashut_curse for about four years). (Restored from the old grand sacrifice results.)

title: A Sorcerer-Prophet of Hashut
summary: Hashut grants a devoted servant mastery of the Winds of Magic. About one chance in four per five years, more for the pious.

title: The Sorcerer's Curse
summary: The sorcerer's flesh turns to black stone: first hands and feet, then the body (incapable), then the head, and the sorcerer joins the stone statues along the roads to Zharr-Naggrund. Sorcery cannot save a sorcerer from this last step. antideath_effect.

title: A K'daai is bound
summary: A daemon summoning ends with a K'daai Fireborn held in the circle.

title: A K'daai bound for another
summary: The sorcerer learns that the K'daai they summoned for their liege is bound.

title: Slave raid
summary: A Chaos Dwarf takes an enemy capital in a chaos_dwarf_slaver_raid war. The first such capital of the war fills a slave building at home; later ones only bring captives and plunder. Or the captives go into Hashut's furnaces. Up to five courtiers of the raided court are dragged off or burned. on_siege_over_winner.

title: Yearly upkeep of a Chaos Dwarf realm
summary: Hidden. Starts Hashut's seven-year sacrifice clock for a new ruler, asks for an overdue sacrifice (dawizharr.8) and herds slave buildings outside the capital to it (dawizharr.32).

title: The slaves are herded to the capital
summary: Slave buildings stand only in the capital. Those elsewhere (after the capital moved, or with a newly gained holding) are torn down, and each lost level adds a level at the capital.

title: The factory slaves die off
summary: Smoke, accidents and hunger thin the factory slaves: the factory loses a level (never below 1). About 1 in 26 per decade, far more often under a poor steward.

title: The levy slaves die off
summary: Brutal hobgoblin overseers and hunger thin the slave levy: it loses a level (never below 1). Same odds as dawizharr.33.

title: Fresh slaves arrive
summary: Slaves paid for an arms deal reach the capital: the ruler puts them in the factory or the levy pens.

title: Sold into slavery
summary: A prisoner is sold in the slave markets. The price follows their best skill. Any slaver may use it since the slavery rework, and may put the prisoner in the pens instead (one lot, WHG_slavery_effects.txt). chaos_dwarf_sell_into_slavery.

title: The slave's fate
summary: The sold captive will be worked to death. Their kin hate the seller.

title: What will you buy?
summary: The buyer picks arms and armour or a battery of war machines (Hellcannons from the Dawi Zharr, cannons and Organ Guns from the Dawi). buy_from_chaos_dwarfs, buy_from_dwarfs and by dawizharr.45 and chaoshorde.21.

title: A buyer at the gates
summary: The seller hears the order. The AI always sells.

title: The price
summary: The buyer pays 150 gold, or (to the Dawi Zharr) chains up people of their capital, hands over slaves from their pits or gives up a prisoner.

title: Payment received
summary: The seller takes the gold, the slaves (put to work, dawizharr.35) or the prisoner, and ships the goods.

title: The goods arrive
summary: War machines come with a guard regiment and wait at the capital; arms and armour equip the capital's levies for ten years. A seller who likes the buyer (opinion 50+) may add a Hellforged Greatshield (1 in 4, once in the buyer's lifetime, dawizharr_greatshield).

title: A Chaos Dwarf offers wares
summary: Hidden step for the sell_stuff_chaos_dwarfs decision: hands the deal to the buyer as if they had asked.

title: The Blood God's contempt
summary: A brave but feeble follower of Khorne is told to prove himself. Accepting starts three rounds of single combat (khorne.2); refusing makes him weak.

title: A challenger
summary: The foe of the round stands before the follower: a young warrior of his own people, then a berserker of Khorne, then a Bloodletter. Fighting starts a duel and the result is judged in 15 days (khorne.3). Turning away ends the trial: the first time it makes him weak, later only costs piety.

title: The duel is over (hidden)
summary: A dead foe is a skull for Khorne: on to the next round, or the god's blessing after the third (khorne.6). A beaten foe still breathes: the follower may finish him (khorne.4). A foe left standing ends the trial (khorne.5).

title: The foe lies bleeding
summary: Taking the skull wins the round; sparing the foe ends the trial in shame. The skull of a berserker may be kept.

title: Khorne turns away
summary: The foe walked away from the duel. Khorne has no use for a fight without a corpse; the trial is over.

title: The Blood God's blessing
summary: The third skull is taken. The follower is made strong and marked by Khorne; a lord without a daemon blade may, once in his life, find the Bloodletter's blade left in the gore.

title: Valkia comes
summary: Valkia the Bloody carries the dead warrior to Khorne's halls.

title: Crippled
summary: A crippled follower of Nurgle broods over his lot. Every month he falls further (nurgle.2 - nurgle.5) until the Grandfather speaks (nurgle.6).

title: Bargaining
summary: You cling to every scrap of strength you have left. Perhaps one of the gods still listens? What if you offered them gold, slaves, anything you own...

title: Despair
summary: Your strength has deserted you and hope has abandoned you. All is lost. Too weak even to speak aloud, you lie and wonder how much time you have left.

title: The Grandfather speaks
summary: Embracing Nurgle heals the body and lifts the despair (nurgle.7); refusing him leaves the sufferer to his end, at peace (nurgle.8).

title: Plaguelord
summary: The Grandfather's gifts: his plagues, which no longer hurt, his mark on a lord of his faith and new strength.

title: Acceptance
summary: You have turned your back on the Grandfather's gift. Now you close your eyes and wait for the end, and for the first time in months you feel at peace.

title: Inspiration
summary: Tzeentch shows a slow-witted follower glimpses of the threads of fate. Careful study makes him smart three times in four; reaching for everything makes him brilliant a little more often than not. Failure leaves him dull, or an imbecile and disfigured, and risks a mutation. Turning away makes him craven and content.

title: The daemonette's counsel (hidden)
summary: A lord who wants to shed a virtue for Slaanesh and keeps a daemonette close hears her out (darkprince.2) once during the ambition. Without one, he may hunt for one (darkprince.10) and looks again in a year or two.

title: Long sensual nights
summary: Giving in sheds one of the virtues the ambition marked, more surely for a zealous or ambitious lord or a clever daemonette. Refusing costs piety and may make the lord diligent.

title: Jaded
summary: A follower of Slaanesh who has tasted every pleasure finds none of them moves him any more, until whispers from beyond promise more. He can set his cult to prepare a summoning (darkprince.11), or shut the whispers out. Once per life. a lord on the shed-a-virtue ambition has no daemonette to counsel him.

title: Through the veil
summary: The cult has gathered all that is needed and something tears through from the other side. Calling it forth brings a daemonette of Slaanesh to court, loyal to the lord. He can still close the tear.

summary: Fired by nurgle_blessing_check_effect (wh_scripted_effects.txt) when a disease strikes the Everchosen, a Nurgle cultist, a Pestilens Skaven, a follower of Nurgle or a plague bearer. The text names the disease.

title: The settlement stands
summary: The camp has outlasted the Wastes: turn it into a city (trade) or a castle (war), with walls, barracks and a market or town. If the province already has both, the camp stays a camp.

title: Clansmen flock to the settlement
summary: Word of the camp spreads and warriors join the horde.

title: A young warrior raises a band
summary: A warrior of the camp gathers followers and rises in revolt.

title: The chieftain is murdered
summary: A champion of one of the gods kills the chieftain. The ruler can take the killer's oath and let them rule the camp, or have them put to death and leave the camp to the chieftain's heir.

title: The settlement is abandoned
summary: A camp without a chieftain to govern it (three years held above baron rank) falls to rubble and is torn down.

title: Karag Dum falls
summary: Hidden. When a siege in the duchy of Karag Dum ends, the winner's top liege decides the hold's fate (chaoshorde.21) if they now hold all of it. Fired from on_siege_over_winner.

title: The fate of Karag Dum
summary: A Chaos ruler who controls all of Karag Dum chooses: burn the hold and take it (A), hand it to a Dawi Zharr governor who sells its people as slaves (B), or burn it and leave it to four champions of the gods (C). Each god likes a different choice. Every power nearby hears of it (chaoshorde.22).

title: News of Karag Dum
summary: Rulers of the Old World, the Wastes, the dwarf holds and nearby greenskins hear that Karag Dum has fallen. Dwarfs swear a grudge against the conqueror and the Dawi Zharr governor; others may fear the conqueror.

title: A building burns in the siege
summary: Dispatcher: one building of the taken holding is lost (chaoshorde.37). Fired from on_siege_over_winner (random list).

title: The warriors run riot
summary: Dispatcher: a holding without buildings is razed (chaoshorde.33); one with buildings is sacked (chaoshorde.34). Strict orders spare an empty holding. Fired from on_siege_over_winner (random list).

title: The town is put to the torch
summary: Dispatcher for settled holdings (not tribal or nomad): an empty one is razed (chaoshorde.33), one with buildings burns (chaoshorde.35). Strict orders spare it. Fired from on_siege_over_winner (random list).

title: Nothing left to occupy
summary: The holding is razed to the ground. The Dark Gods take note (doom), and the warriors may bring back a trophy (1 in 50, once in a lifetime).

title: The holding is sacked
summary: Notification: two buildings are lost and the holding is sacked for a year.

title: The town burns
summary: Notification: four buildings are lost and the holding burns (two years).

title: Your holding is ruined
summary: Notification for the owner of a sacked or razed holding.

title: A building burns
summary: Notification: one building of the taken holding is lost.

title: Orders for the captured towns
summary: The ruler tells the warriors how to treat the holdings they take for the next two years: lax, normal, strict, or no mercy (in a holy war, or for a zealous or wrathful ruler).

title: Slaughter
summary: Dispatcher under lax or no-mercy orders only: an empty holding is razed (chaoshorde.33), one with buildings is gutted (chaoshorde.40). Fired from on_siege_over_winner (random list).

title: The town is gutted
summary: Notification: eight buildings are lost and the holding burns (two years).

title: Razed to the ground
summary: Dispatcher under lax or no-mercy orders: any holding but a capital is razed (chaoshorde.33), buildings or not. Rare. Fired from on_siege_over_winner (random list).

title: The warlord is dead
summary: Hidden. Starts the break-up for the heir. Fired from on_death.

title: The tribes break away
summary: A duchy outside the capital's, bordering a foreign realm, breaks off under a new warlord (chaoshorde.52), and the heir is asked again until their prestige holds the rest (the bar drops with every duchy lost). A player can follow a breakaway warlord instead.

title: The warlord binds a warband
summary: As chaoshorde.53, for one neighbouring warband.

title: The breakaway settles
summary: Hidden. After 50 days a breakaway warband can no longer be bound by its neighbours.

title: The kingdoms break away
summary: As chaoshorde.51, by kingdom: any province outside the capital's kingdom can break off, and the heir needs less prestige to hold the rest.

title: A coward's answer

summary: The loser's last moments: they die by the winner's hand (unless invincible). The winner then faces the next challenger (chaosfl.14) or, if none is left, is crowned champion (chaosfl.15).

title: Who's next?
summary: The winner dedicates the blood to Khorne and calls out the next challenger (chaosfl.8).

title: Champion of the Blood God

title: Called off
summary: Too few challengers came. Notification for the challengers who did, who lose Khorne's favour; cleanup follows (chaosfl.17).

title: Fearless
summary: The champion becomes brave, or sharper in war if already brave.

summary: The champion becomes wroth, or sharper in war if already wroth.

title: Khorne watches

summary: Hidden. When a champion, chosen or daemon prince of Chaos dies, the doom recedes: a little for a champion, more for a chosen, most for a prince. Fired from on_death.

title: Invitation to be tested
summary: The head of the college invites the applicant to be tested for the gift.

title: The testing
summary: The examiners measure the applicant's gift. Anyone with the gift, hidden or known, is admitted to the examiner's college and goes on to choose a wind (college.20, fired by join_magic_society_effect).

title: AI mages join and rise
summary: On the five-year pulse an AI ruler who is a member may rise a rank (1 in 4, up to Lord Magister), trained AI mages at his court (and he himself) may join a college, AI Lord Magisters may challenge a player Patriarch of their wind (college_ai_challenge_effect), and AI members buy one item from the stores (college_ai_store_effect). Which colleges are near is worked out once per ruler (college_mark_near_effect).

title: Choose a wind (Gold, Bright, Amethyst, Grey)
summary: A new member who is not yet a wizard picks the wind he will study; the AI picks at random. Two more pages follow (college.21, college.22).

title: Choose a wind (Amber, Celestial)
summary: Now that you have been accepted into , you must choose the Order you will join. Since Teclis taught the first wizards of the Empire, every Imperial wizard...

title: Choose a wind (Light, Jade)
summary: Now that you have been accepted into , you must choose the Order you will join. Since Teclis taught the first wizards of the Empire, every Imperial wizard...

title: Finding a teacher
summary: Looks for a Magister (rank 3 or more) of the student's wind, preferring AI Magisters with fewer than three apprentices and plain Magisters over Lord Magisters. Sets found_teacher_in_college when one is found.

title: Meeting the teacher
summary: The student meets his teacher, or learns that no Magister of his wind can take him and he must study alone. Studying alone is harder but stands out (prestige, and more college currency when he finishes). A player may also go back and pick another wind.

title: A student is assigned
summary: Tells a player Magister that a new student has been placed with him.

title: A teacher dies
summary: When a Magister dies, each of his college students who has not finished is flagged and given a new teacher (college.23).

title: How to make a name
summary: A Journeyman (political_focus_college) picks how he will rise: through patrons, through research or on the battlefield. Replaces his lifestyle trait. The AI picks by its best skill.

title: Relay for favouritism_colleges (hidden)
summary: A targeted decision's event has the target as ROOT and FROM, so the decision fires this in the patron's scope instead, and it sends college.40 to the member with the patron as FROM.

title: A patron offers a promotion
summary: A Lord Magister (favouritism_colleges) offers to have a lesser member promoted for a favour. Accepting raises the member a rank and puts him in the patron's debt (or cancels a favour the patron owed him).

title: The offer is accepted
summary: ,I gladly accept your help, and I will not forget it.Signed,

title: The offer is refused
summary: The patron's influence is not spent (refunded in college.40).

title: Challenge the Patriarch
summary: A player Lord Magister whose wind already has a Patriarch, with every Patriarch's seat filled, may challenge him to a duel of spells before the Order. The challenge costs as much as the rank itself.

title: The duel is fought
summary: A duel of spells, not of swords: the odds follow the magic power, gift, learning and focus of both wizards, with the sitting Patriarch slightly favoured. The loser may be burned by a miscast.

title: The challenger wins
summary: The Patriarch steps down to Lord Magister and the challenger takes his seat. Once in a while the beaten wizard is burned by his own miscast.

title: The Patriarch wins
summary: The challenger is beaten before the Order. He keeps a little of the currency he spent and cannot challenge again for 600 days.

title: A Lord Magister challenges you
summary: An AI Lord Magister of the player Patriarch's wind demands a duel of spells for the seat (college_ai_challenge_effect). Accept the duel, step down, or spend college currency to have the challenge quashed.

title: Defending the seat
summary: The same duel of spells as college.51, seen from the Patriarch's side.

title: The Articles of Imperial Magic
summary: Announces a new college to the founder, his vassals and every player. The founder gets the legal-magic bloodline.

title: The college stores
summary: A trained member from Journeyman up (college_equipment_requisition) visits the stores and spends college currency on the tools of his art. Each item can be held once; better pieces need a higher rank.

title: Battle stores
summary: The Power Stone of the member's wind (one active at a time), staffs and rings of power by rank.

title: Robes and regalia
summary: Robes of the Order and warding amulets, better by rank, and the Patriarch's circlet for the heads of the Orders.

title: Study
summary: The grimoire of the member's own wind, from Magister up, and eyeglasses for close work.

title: Relay for request_college_house (hidden)
summary: Fired in the wizard's scope so that college.80 reaches the liege with the wizard as FROM (see college.39).

title: The court wizard asks for a house
summary: A landless Lord Magister or Patriarch (request_college_house) asks his liege to give his Order a house in the liege's capital. Granting it adds the local college building and wins the wizard's gratitude; Sigmarite zealots and lands where magic is outlawed are less willing. A refusal refunds the wizard.

title: The house is granted
summary: ,The shall have its house in . See that it does nothing to make me regret it.

title: The house is refused
summary: ,I have considered your request and must refuse it. The common folk already mutter about witchcraft at my court, and I will not give them a building to point...

title: Flavour picker
summary: On the society bi-yearly pulse a trained college member may get one small flavour event: one for his own Order (Bright, Gold, Celestial) or the feast of the Orders, which anyone may get. About one member in eight per pulse, so roughly once in fifteen years each.

title: Singed
summary: A Bright wizard's experiment with Aqshy goes the way most of them do: loudly. Pay for the damage, blame the apprentice, or write it up as a success.

title: Lead into gold
summary: A Gold wizard tries the oldest trick of alchemy. It might work, it might blow up, or he can sell the "gold" to someone who knows less than he does.

title: Written in the stars
summary: A Celestial wizard reads a sign in the heavens. Proclaim it from the tower and stake his name on it, whisper it to his liege, or keep it for the Order's star charts.

title: The feast of the Orders
summary: The college dines together and two Magisters of rival Orders start a quarrel across the table, with sparks. Take your Order's side, make the peace, or pocket the silver while everyone is watching the fight.

title: The court changes
summary: Hidden, players only. Once a year a player's court shifts a little on its own: a dull courtier finds a talent or loses one (1 in 4), two lonely courtiers become lovers, friends or rivals (1 in 4, or 1 in 2 with many lonely courtiers), a courtier gains a passing modifier (3 in 10) and one without a nickname earns one (1 in 10). The four vanilla events (61001 - 61004) used break = yes; they are one event now. Fixed: the talent loss checked the ruler's skills, not the courtier's; lovers were only made between courtiers who disliked each other, and could be close kin.

title: A name of one's own
summary: A courtier without a nickname begs the player for one. A fine name pleases them (it costs prestige to hand out honours), a plain one is neutral, a cruel one stings. The text follows the courtier's best skill. Fixed: the "fair" and "handsome" names checked the ruler's sex, not the courtier's; the fourth name of each kind was never given.

title: Time to go

Three to five courtiers who matter to no one take their leave, with their spouses and children at court; the ruler pays them off or keeps them. Fixed: a courtier with any one child outside the ruler's family could go even if another child was the ruler's own or heir; now no child of theirs may be.

title: A crowded hall
summary: A courtier of a full court (court limit rule on) jokes that the ruler keeps a crowded but happy hall. Brush it off as a fool, smile like a schemer who knows numbers are strength, make it an act of charity or of cruelty, or say every one of them matters (prestige, piety, kindness). Each answer is a host reputation for 15 years. Independent rulers and players only.
